claim: readSpan validates a span by hashing the presented bytes and comparing to contentHash rather than trusting the start/end offsets, so a span whose start/end have been moved to a different location within the same underlying bytes still reads successfully as long as the byte content still hashes the same.
The attach pointer for a CasObject is asserted to have exactly one own key, 'hash', with no other metadata such as size or role carried alongside it.

In the guardrail test, a content-hash miss combined with a nodeKey hit routes to UPDATE for the advisory family but to SUPERSEDE for the predicate family (with checkSame true), so routeWrite's outcome depends on family, not just on the hash/nodeKey hit pattern alone.

The test deliberately does not assert what verdict the malformed JSON-array-scope write receives (it only checks the exit code is 0, 1, or 2); it only requires that a subsequent legitimate write to the same anchor still succeeds and is not rejected for a governance-relocation reason.

storeWithRivalOnFirstCommit only injects the rival sidecar write on the FIRST call to commitStaging (guarded by a `commits === 1` counter), so later commits in the same test run against the real, unmodified store.

facetOf distinguishes a ConventionsSource from a plausible README-like object solely by the presence of an `anchor` field, not by the presence of a `path` field, so an object with `path` but no `anchor` still yields UN-SEEDED rather than being treated as a conventions source.
When a decayed fact re-enters via logHit, its hit count resets to 1 rather than resuming from the count it had before decay.

labelCoChanged unconditionally overwrites the relation field to 'coChanged' on every surviving fact, discarding whatever original relation kind (e.g. dependency/dependent) that fact carried before being placed in the coChanged band.

In splitBands, once one T2 row fails to fit under ADVISORY_CAP the capped flag is set permanently, so every later T2 row is dropped even if its own claim.length would still fit in the remaining budget, rather than the fill trying smaller later rows against the leftover space.
The `pullOptimize` fallback path re-materializes the pack from scratch on every call rather than caching or memoizing it across invocations.
When the required `scope` argument is omitted from an atlas-negations call, the resulting error text contains the exact lowercase substring "missing scope" rather than a generic validation message.

The AC-4 back-compat test does not just assert row.seal is undefined, it also asserts the seal key is truly absent from the row object via hasOwnProperty, so an implementation that sets seal: undefined would pass the first assertion but fail this stricter one.

In the v2 negation door, when a target-escape site and a dynamic-reach channel are both present, the abstention reason returned is escape-open, not scope-dynamic, showing the door checks the escape leg before the dynamic-reach leg.

The live-path admission test deliberately supplies a StructRef with a stale, mismatched subtreeHash for the existing file 'src/util.ts' and the gate still emits, showing that admission is decided by reground re-deriving the hash rather than by trusting the candidate's recorded subtreeHash.

verifyNegation treats scope containment segment-wise rather than as a string prefix, so a caller or hole in a sibling directory whose name merely starts with the scope string (e.g. src/paycheck relative to scope src/pay) does not count as being under that scope for either the refute or the proven/abstain checks.

In SCN-TOOLS-10c-1, storeNodes.resolve only matches address A ('cas:9b21'), but the governed store write uses key g.key = id(N1) (a different NodeKey/Hash), so resolveNode(A, t) never resolves against the written value and the write-refusal loop exercises only the no-node-resolved fail-closed path rather than a genuinely resolved node.

The invoke() helper calls commitProjection and commitStaging with a decision-function argument, persistProjection with a projection object argument, and every other listed door with no arguments at all, so the flat door lists hide three distinct call signatures.

When both .atlas/staging.json and the projection+cas files are committed together, the test asserts the query still refuses with REJECTED_UNTRUSTED_STORE rather than falling back to serving the projection-backed data.

The exhaustive coverage test iterates over all combinations of withCheck, seedNode, and seedCas (2x2x2=8 cells) and asserts writeDecision always returns one of DEDUP/CREATE/UPDATE/SUPERSEDE, never a REJECT or a thrown error, for any family x hit-state combination.

The PROP-KERNEL-11 event generator (eventSpecArb) is deliberately built as fc.uniqueArray without a selector, so events can collide on the same contentHash with a different `fresh` flag, and this collision case is what actually exercises the fold's convergence property.

the concurrent pool clips its batch width to the remaining budget room left at the ceiling rather than dispatching a full-width batch and discarding the overshoot, so paid-for calls exactly equal used calls even when the ceiling is not a multiple of POOL_WIDTH.

deserialize only checks that the parsed object's trailer property is a non-null object; it does not validate that any of the trailer's individual fields are present, so a trailer missing required fields still passes and yields a non-null Dossier.
crossesThreshold uses a strict greater-than comparison, so when the off-atlas rate exactly equals theta (e.g. rate 0.30 with theta 0.3) the threshold is NOT considered crossed.

The test suite pins an accepted asymmetry between families: hyphen-joined non-secret text right after a Slack token gets absorbed into the [REDACTED] placeholder, but the identical hyphen-joined pattern right after a GitHub token is left intact outside the placeholder, since '-' terminates a GitHub body but is itself a valid Slack body character.

The admission door emits two distinct shapes of refusal message for index-query checks: an unknown operator gets the full operator menu, while a known operator with a bad argument gets only that operator's own expected form.

TransitionProposal is the only concrete kind in the Proposal union that has no `site: Candidate` field, carrying `unitKey: string` instead where every other proposal kind (predicate, advisory, relation, negation) anchors on a ranked `site`.

The test asserts that five distinct write commands (derive-relations, emit, link, promote, transition) collapse onto only two distinct legs in COMMAND_LEG, so the write-command count and the write-door count are deliberately different and the test checks the mapped-door SET equals WRITE_PATHS rather than checking a 1:1 command-to-door correspondence.
resolveBySubtreeAt refuses to answer (returns undefined) whenever a content hash matches more than one distinct path in the rev's tree, rather than arbitrarily picking the first match.

Re-asserting an already-linked pair through the door succeeds each time and publishes a fresh generation on every call (three redundant calls produce three new persisted entries), even though the resulting stored content is byte-identical to the previous generation, whereas the analogous re-retraction of an already-retracted pair is refused outright and persists nothing.

In decideStaging, only a negation fact keeps its own scope field untouched and instead gets a separate authzScope stamped to MINED_SCOPE, whereas advisory, predicate, and relation facts have their scope field itself overwritten with MINED_SCOPE.

The test verifies Tree-handle release by monkey-patching TreeProto.delete (the prototype obtained dynamically via Object.getPrototypeOf on a throwaway parse) to count calls, so it mutates a prototype shared process-wide rather than mocking a per-instance method or an imported function.
EMPTY_ROOT is computed at test-run time by calling build() with an empty children array rather than being pinned as a hardcoded hash literal.

The narrowing guard in git-drift checks whether the recorded path still resolves at the new revision BEFORE falling back to the subtree-hash lookup, so a duplicate-content match at an earlier-sorting path is never reached when the original path is still present, preventing a phantom rename pair.
writeWithScanner rejects a scanner whose name is the empty string by throwing an error matching /NAMED scanner/, even when that scanner's scan function would report a clean result.

isGrounded treats an entry as ungrounded whenever its subtreeHash coerces to an empty string, so a grounding with any empty subtreeHash among otherwise well-formed entries fails the check for the whole grouping, not just that entry.

admitToBuffer treats a buffer whose identity is not already tracked in its WeakMap as having up to MAX_SEAM_CARRY trailing provisional bytes rather than assuming zero carry, so a buffer built or resumed by a caller outside this module is re-examined over the widest possible split-credential window instead of being trusted as already clean.
The disk store in this test is constructed with a hash function that always returns asHash('seed') regardless of the value being stored, so every seeded row is put under the identical content hash.

The round-trip assertion uses toBe (reference identity) rather than toEqual, implying the store's get(hash) is expected to return the exact same in-memory object instance that was put, not a deserialized copy.

The post-fix reconcile predicate built inline in this test classifies a moved fact as mechanical by looking only at the subtreeHash of the fact's first grounding entry's anchor and checking it via resolveBySubtreeAt at the new revision, not by comparing the anchor's path at all.
scrubGrounding scrubs only qualifiedPath and path on each grounding entry, deliberately leaving subtreeHash, kind, displayLines, and span untouched.

The two memory-never-deleted guards use different failure shapes: a hard-delete on the rules store throws, while a non-orchestrator logbook append is silently refused, returning the unchanged log rather than throwing.

seedAwareness always renders the mission facet as UN-SEEDED unconditionally, without ever checking the ratified list for a DEFINE artifact or calling missionStub, so passing a ratified DEFINE fact in the `ratified` array has no effect on the mission facet.

In the atlas-query leg, the config.readRefusal check runs before the --by mode split, so both the default scope path and the dependency/trigger retrieval modes are refused identically rather than only the scope path being guarded.
makeQueryDb memoizes its builder callback so that calling .get() many times (30 in this test) invokes the supplied builder function only once, returning the same cached db object thereafter.

enrichEnabled treats any set value not matching one of the recognized falsey spellings as truthy (the test pins an arbitrary string like 'symbol' as ON), so it works as a denylist of falsey spellings rather than an allowlist of truthy ones.

gateWithPresent's gateHolds narrows on node.kind === 'advisory' before reading claimNorm in the same boolean expression, so a non-advisory GroundedFact (e.g. a PredicateNode without claimNorm) short-circuits to NA rather than reading an undefined field into the present-set check.

Before exercising the leak, the test first asserts that folding tree A and tree B each independently yield a non-empty prior-key set and that those two sets are mutually disjoint, so the later leak assertions cannot pass vacuously on empty or overlapping keys.

The two tests check occurrence roles through different representations of the same fixture: the first decodes the real serialized SCIP protobuf and tests the SymbolRole.Definition bitflag, while the second reads expectedScipOutput's plain 'definition'/'reference' string field directly, without going through deserializeSCIP.

bindReconcile computes exitCode as strictly 2 when semantic is non-empty and 0 otherwise, so the returned exitCode can only ever be 0 or 2, never any other value, regardless of how large the drifted or mechanical sets are.

routeWrite's decision precedence, independently re-derived from the 16-cell input product in this test, is contentHash-hit first, then nodeKey-miss, then advisory family always UPDATE regardless of checkSame, then predicate family branching on checkSame between SUPERSEDE and CREATE.

the baseline PPR ranking (rankedPaths) is computed once via a driveMine call placed directly in the describe block's body, not inside an it(), so its result is shared as a fixed constant across both tests in that describe rather than being recomputed per test.
The reconcile output preserves the original input pair order rather than grouping items by mechanical/semantic classification.

Even past the split floor where the whole credential is no longer reconstructible, an unredacted tail fragment of the secret still survives raw in the second stored object, because that fragment has no prefix to mark it as a credential.
The parser accepts `--depth=notanumber` and any other non-numeric value for the `--depth` flag without validation or throwing, folding it as a plain string just like every other unknown flag.

The fast-check arbitrary for nodeKey uses fc.option with `nil: undefined` rather than omitting the property, because the content() builder's opts type requires nodeKey to be present-and-undefined under exactOptionalPropertyTypes rather than simply optional.

The fallback reasons for a reasonless fail-closed write are asymmetric: an emit failure appends a parenthetical "(ungrounded)" to its message while the link failure's fallback message carries no such qualifier.

Test (v) shows the forged .scip dump changes the dependency-mode query's blast-radius output (edges appear or vanish with the forged dump), while the scope-based 'query src' door returns the same claims regardless of either forged dump, so freshness-gating and dependency-edge derivation read the same forgeable input but only one of them is defended against it.

EpicUnit's declared shape carries only an id, a goal string, and a features array of OwnUnit, with no NodeKey or anchor field, so it is structurally incapable of being treated as a grounded scope-unit.

The bound recompute function reads the node's own `grounding` field directly (passing node.grounding as the second argument to gate.gateHolds) even though it never reads the node's `status` field, so the fact's self-reported grounding is trusted as an input while only its self-reported status verdict is discarded.

A poisoned value placed inside the fact's grounding field (e.g. a BigInt on grounding.seq) is rejected with reason 'unaddressable-cas-object' rather than 'canonical-form violation', distinguishing it from the other SHAPES-driven poisoned-field test cases that all report 'canonical-form violation'.

resolveFrontier conditionally spreads prior into the returned FrontierOptions only when unitPriorOf returns a defined value, so the prior key is entirely absent from the object (not present with value undefined) when the skeleton source has no unit-prior seam.

buildDynamicReach treats an unparseable TS file and an unscanned JS-family file (.cjs/.mjs/.js/.jsx) both as positive channel witnesses (fail-closed), while a genuinely different-language file such as .py is instead skipped and contributes no witness at all.

The tier bound is tested against strings like 'toString', '__proto__', and 'constructor' as OFF_LATTICE inputs, verifying atLeastT1 does membership checks against the tier lattice rather than relying on inherited Object prototype properties or JS coercion.

createCasIndex's put() only adds the returned hash to the drift-eligibility registry when the kernel store returns a truthy hash, so a malformed object that yields the kernel's empty handle is stored without becoming drift-eligible.

makeGateFix writes .atlas/index.scip into the repo and calls scip.cleanup() immediately afterward, so the fixture's SCIP source is deleted while the copied file inside repoPath remains for the test to use.

the join between a fact's declared tier and its derived tier is one-directional: a derived T0 forces a declared T2 candidate into full-ratify, but a derived T2 never relaxes a declared T0 candidate's gate, which already routes to full-ratify on its own.
logHit performs a runtime check that nodeId is a non-empty string and throws a TypeError if not, even though NodeKey is already typed as a string.

When a ForgedOccurrence omits its range, forgedScipBytes silently defaults it to [0, 0, 0, 0] rather than leaving the field absent, so range-omission tests actually encode a degenerate zero-range occurrence.

In makeFixture, the .atlas/index.scip file that composeRuntime's index build reads is copied in only after both git commits are made and is never `git add`-ed, so it deliberately stays outside the fixture repo's tracked git history while still being present on disk.

rowAuthorized falls back to the stored fact's scope only when the projection row's own scope is undefined; when the row does carry a scope it is used even if it differs from the stored fact's scope, and that mismatch is instead caught separately by rowContradicted.

In mineWhyEmpty, the incomplete-pass check runs before the sitesVisited===0 check, so a pass that both failed to complete AND visited 0 sites reports the completion-cause message, never the frontier-empty explanation.

NegationNode.grounding is typed as the general Grounding type (which is not cardinality-restricted in this file), so the 'exactly one entry, anchored at the scope directory' invariant described in the comment is not enforced by the TypeScript type itself and must be checked at runtime by whatever constructs this node.
redispatch's returned object carries only kind and seatId, never the brief itself, even though the brief is what was hashed to produce seatId.

meterApi.meter accepts completely non-object inputs — including undefined, null, the number 42, and a bare string — without throwing, and still returns a Metering record with every required field defined rather than a partial or undefined-filled record.

The ENRICH round filters its item list by the bornFromWorkLazy flag before calling relate(), silently skipping any item marked bornFromWorkLazy:true rather than passing every item in the list through the loop.

driftDetect returns an identical verdict for two groundings that differ only in their displayLines field, confirming the drift decision is computed purely from subtreeHash and never reads the displayLines navigation hint.

mintPack sorts the invariant rows by nodeId before calling splitBands, so which rows survive the advisory band's truncation cap is determined by nodeId ordering rather than by the order pairs were passed in.

The G-GAP2-7 test proves a comment sitting between two declarations is bound to the declaration that follows it, not the one it trails, by asserting the edit drifts function b (following) while explicitly asserting it does NOT drift function a (preceding).

canonicalForm sorts object keys at every nesting depth, not just the top level: the fixture declares nested keys as {b, a} but the pinned preimage assertion expects them serialized in the order {a, b}.

resolves() returns true for a symbol that is defined but has zero references (no callers), the same empty-callers result a phantom (referenced-but-undefined) symbol also produces, so callers-empty alone cannot distinguish a resolvable-but-uncalled symbol from a phantom — only resolves() can.
hasLine matches a line by exact trimmed-string equality rather than substring search, so a commented-out or otherwise-modified occurrence of the pattern does not count as already present.

proposeAll dispatches every candidate's message up front via slot % seats.length with no back-pressure, so when the batch is larger than the worker width, some workers are queued multiple jobs at once rather than the pool waiting for a worker to free up before assigning its next job.

scrubGrounding redacts credential-shaped text only in the anchor's qualifiedPath and the entry's human path, leaving the anchor's subtreeHash and kind fields byte-for-byte untouched even when the same token string appears embedded in both the redacted and unredacted fields.
TS_TYPE_CTX deliberately omits as_expression and satisfies_expression, so isSafe treats the operand of an `X as T` cast as an escaping reference rather than a runtime-erased type position.

The test's `set()` fixture builder dedupes by event id using a has-guard, so when two events share an id the FIRST one passed wins and later duplicates are silently dropped rather than overwriting it.

A predicate fact whose check literally contains the secret and one whose check already has the redacted placeholder both resolve to the identical nodeKey and identical contentHash, so decideStaging cannot distinguish an already-scrubbed check from one that had a live secret scrubbed out of it.
An uncovered path defaults to a deny verdict only when it shares a directory with a T0 territory member; an uncovered path elsewhere defaults to an open verdict instead.

createReconcile is constructed with only a DriftSource and a KNOW-5 classifier — no store, writer, or adapter dependency is injected — so even when options.acceptReground is true, the function only counts the mechanical subset into regroundedCount and performs no actual write of its own.

The negation fixture used in this suite deliberately targets a global-looking symbol ('scip:Nowhere#', not a `local `-prefixed one) so the test exercises the deps-completeness gate specifically, rather than tripping an earlier target-not-global abstention first.

The DETERMINISM test's expected tiebreak winner is 'from-padded' because the sort's ascending lexicographic comparison on filename ranks "projection.007.json" before "projection.7.json" (the character '0' sorts before '7'), regardless of which file was written first.

underScope compares the anchor's file-path segments (split on '/', taken before the first '::') against the scope's segments position by position, so a scope of 'sr' would NOT match an anchor path beginning with 'src' even though a raw string startsWith('sr') would.

In stagingFake's commitStaging, when the decision's next is undefined the function returns immediately before the loop that puts decision.put objects into the CAS, so a refused/no-op decision writes neither the projection nor any CAS bytes even if the decision specified objects to put.

SCN-INDEX-6b-1 verifies the absence of a fourth retrieval mode not just by type but at runtime: it checks 'search' is not an own property via `in`, reads it with Reflect.get to confirm it is undefined, and asserts byTrigger('search:acme') returns an empty array rather than treating the string as a free-text query.

composedGate resolves and memoizes the gate lazily on first emit rather than eagerly at construction, so a repo whose SkeletonSource frontier is empty never triggers buildMineAdmission or an index read.

mergeAtlas does not merge ours, theirs, and an optional base in one combined operation; it first unions ours and theirs, and only then, if base is supplied, folds base into that already-unioned result via a second merge call.
isPositiveInt requires atLeast to be an integer of 1 or more, so a claim with atLeast set to 0 is rejected as malformed rather than being treated as a trivially-true lower bound.

Flagging a territory as a t0Candidate never rewrites its tier or blastRadius: even territories matched by the T0 heuristic remain tier T2 with the identical territories/blastRadius as when no heuristic fires, so t0Candidates is purely an informational flag with zero promotions in this suite.

The reconcile CLI treats an empty-string merge-base argument the same as a malformed sha or a well-formed-but-absent sha: all three produce a non-zero exit and a reason line containing 'unresolvable-merge-base:' rather than being special-cased or silently defaulting.
The test asserts that omitting `--by` entirely produces stdout byte-identical to an explicit `--by scope` call, pinning the default mode as scope for backward compatibility.

Both cache-teeth fixtures deliberately pick a second document/symbol/tool name that changes the encoded byte length, and assert that length difference before writing, so the test cannot pass merely by relying on filesystem mtime granularity moving between writes.

The drift() function's returned DriftItem only ever reports the anchorWas/anchorNow pair of the FIRST drifted entry, even when the mechanical repair plan() computes and re-anchors every drifted entry in the grounding, so a caller reading only drift() cannot see how many entries actually moved.

verifyCount's exact-mode world-openness check is segment-wise scoped, so a hole in a sibling directory that only string-prefixes worldScope does not open the world and does not flip a provable exact count into a false scope-open abstention.

In the per-row loop, the try/catch around deps.emit only swallows a DegenerateAnchorError (matched by instanceof or by a duplicated-module name check); any other thrown error propagates out of promote() uncaught and aborts the whole batch rather than being recorded as that row's individual refusal.

importCas only re-derives and verifies the content address for entries whose key matches the 64-hex HASH_SHAPE pattern; any entry filed under a non-hash-shaped key is inserted into the returned Cas verbatim with no integrity check at all.
In COMMAND_LEG, four distinct commands — emit, promote, transition, and derive-relations — all map to the same Leg value 'atlas-emit', not emit alone.

When a WriteRequest omits seal, the test checks not just that the stored row's seal reads undefined but that seal is not even an own property of the row via hasOwnProperty, confirming the field is built with a conditional spread rather than being set to an explicit undefined value.

defaultKind requires BOTH checkable and tier>=T1 to return 'predicate': a checkable T2 signal still resolves to 'advisory' because tier alone fails the conjunction, not because checkability is ignored.

verifyNegation checks isLocal(target) before checking reverse.resolves(target), so a local (document-scoped) target is abstained on ('target-not-global') without ever querying the reverse-callers index.

The test seeds a sameAs edge by mutating a fresh copy of store.current directly (bypassing upsert/WriteRequest) because sameAs is not a field the WriteRequest type carries, so a governed-raise write cannot set it at all.

the `sorted` helper re-keys both the outer nodeKey map and each node's per-entry map in ascending order after folding, so fold()'s returned Map has deterministic own iteration order regardless of input insertion order, not merely a deterministic serialized form.

In reviewRound, enrichRound, and expandRound, the returned value field is always set equal to the round's revisions count, so runLoop's marginal-value stop condition is effectively checking the same number as its fixpoint (revisions===0) check.

freshness() never folds a closure member's full-body subtreeHash, only its interfaceRState, so a callee that undergoes a pure-body refactor with an untouched interface leaves the caller's snapshot FRESH.

The reHashAt fixture predicate fails closed for an unrecognized newSha: when the lookup table has no entry for the given hash, rehashed is undefined and the comparison short-circuits to false (never re-derives/mechanical) rather than throwing or defaulting to true.

promoteVerdict distinguishes a staging read that outright refused (out.read false, exitCode 2, 'status: rejected') from a staging read that succeeded but found zero candidates (exitCode 0, honest empty), rather than collapsing both into the same reported count.

A rewritten commit's note is unreadable even when the notes refspec IS configured (readAfterBareClone(c2,'N',true) is still null), because the orphaning is keyed on the old SHA and is independent of whether notes are fetched.

Querying an unknown scope and emitting under a policy-denied write are both governed refusals but land in different exit-code/status buckets: the unknown-scope query is exit 1 / status: error, while the policy-denied emit is exit 2 / status: rejected.

normalizeForGrammarGaps is proven length-preserving for all three rescued grammar-gap constructs while leaving ordinary code, including a real dynamic import(spec) call and a computed ns[key] access, completely byte-identical.

ground() returns immediately with an empty { entries: [] } as soon as a single citation fails to resolve, discarding any entries already resolved for earlier citations in the same node rather than dropping only the unresolvable one and keeping the rest.

The test fixtures deliberately set the incoming fact's own id field to the sentinel value 'SHOULD-BE-REMINTED' to prove decideStaging ignores the payload-supplied id entirely and recomputes nodeKey from relationKey/negationKey instead of trusting it.

netModel's reverseAnchors parameter (which would reorder file objects to put H.send before H.jfile) is declared with a default of false but is never invoked with true anywhere in this file, so that branch of the fixture is unexercised here.

The WireSeams fixture used in this test stubs isCandidate to always return false and gateHolds to always return 'NA', so the T0 heuristic and truth gate are effectively neutralized and play no role in the freshness behavior this test verifies.
One test enforces that store.ts contains exactly one 'new Map' construction by reading and regex-matching the source file's own text at test time, rather than only asserting on store behavior.

The identity test proves rawAnswer is stripped before hashing: two facts with the same claim, one carrying a rawAnswer and one not, produce byte-identical nodeKey and contentHash, differing only in whether answerRef is defined.
InjectApi.recall closes over the store bound at makeInject construction time rather than taking a store argument, unlike injectFor/assembleHeader/compose which all take store explicitly.

OwnPack.unit is typed as a plain string, distinct in kind from RelationSet.unit which is typed as Path, so the two same-named `unit` fields across these interfaces are not interchangeable despite sharing a name.

produce() returns an empty array both when the moment is off-union (rejected) and when a valid moment is called with an empty event array, so the return value alone cannot distinguish a rejected sweep from a legitimate no-op production.

The dependency axis's per-file subtreeHash is a constant function of the file's path alone (nodeHashOfPath), so editing a file's content changes the spatial axis's hash for that file but leaves the dependency axis's hash for the same file completely unchanged.

createRevIndex's worktree-add retry logic distinguishes a transient lock failure from a permanently bad rev purely by the error signature text ('could not lock ref' / 'Unable to create worktree lock' vs 'invalid reference'), retrying only the lock-signature case and classifying the invalid-reference case as fast-empty on the very first attempt.

createInit's signature takes no LLM/model port at all, so its determinism (two calls to init() returning equal output) is structurally guaranteed rather than merely observed, since there is no seam through which nondeterministic input could enter.

The module-graph audit greps the whole packages directory (which would also match this very test file's own `ModelClient` import) but then filters hits to only paths containing '/src/', so the test's own reference to ModelClient never inflates the count it asserts.

The two content-addressed lookup doors in this suite disagree on miss behavior: the transcript store's fetch() throws on a never-put pointer (fail closed), while the attach surface's get() returns undefined on a never-attached hash (fail soft), even though both are hash-keyed reads over a CAS.

The three retraction refusal discriminants (not-linked, already-retracted, retracted-pair) are constructed so that none is a prefix or substring of another, so a substring-based equality check cannot confuse them.

validateTemplate admits the structured record { claimNorm, grounding: partial2 } as valid even though that same partial2 grounding fails the truth door in the other test in this file, showing validateTemplate performs only a coarse structural check and does not itself verify whether the grounding is actually grounded.

Unlike the other four doctor subcommands (archive/why/hotset/reground), which fail closed with a 'composition-root WP' error when no DoctorSource is injected, the `index` subcommand works fine with no DoctorSource at all because it reads only the file tree and SCIP dump rather than the store.

In makeStoreSpy's fake commitProjection, when the decision's `next` is undefined the function returns immediately without executing the `put` loop, so any objects listed in `decision.put` are silently discarded rather than written to the store.
eagerRehashState(h('A'), edges) never includes A itself in its returned touched set, only nodes reachable within MAX_HOPS reverse-dependency hops from the edited node.

Setting ATLAS_FRONTIER to the misspelled value 'symbols' (plural) is asserted to silently fall back to the default file-level frontier, producing two file-kind sites, rather than erroring or activating the symbol frontier.

gitLsFiles validates a parsed blob oid against a hex regex before it is ever passed to `git cat-file`, specifically to stop a field beginning with '-' from being interpreted by git as a command-line option rather than an object id.

the barrel re-exports its own types module with `export type *` (type-only), while every runtime submodule (gate, emit-guard, subtree, span, drift, freshness, ground) is re-exported with a plain `export *`, so only the types.js exports are guaranteed to carry no runtime values through this barrel.

The minted sub-file unit key embeds the AST node-type label (e.g. arrow_function), which is part of what keeps two identically-shaped sibling closures in the same function from colliding on the same key.

A fact carrying an empty own scope is rejected with reason 'malformed scope' at an earlier gate than the authz check, distinctly not surfaced as 'unauthorized', even though the acting actor would otherwise be authorized.

The archived R13 entry marks its evicted-but-retained state by putting the plain string 'archived' into the ordinary stoppedAt field of a TaskMemoryEntry, not through any dedicated archive/eviction flag on the entry or store shape.

reasonOf extracts a refusal's discriminant by splitting on only the FIRST colon and taking the substring before it, so a rationale paragraph that itself contains additional colons after the name does not corrupt the extracted discriminant.

Both negationsOf and abstentionsOf return results ordered by lexicographic scope string, not by insertion/map order — the fixtures are inserted payments-then-orders but both folds return the orders-scoped row first.

Only the ungrounded-rejection assertion checks that stdout contains the literal invariant citation 'TOOLS-1/7'; the unauthorized-rejection assertion in S2b checks the same structural shape (status/next/invariant/reason lines) but never asserts that specific invariant string, so the two fail-closed paths are not pinned to cite the same invariant text.

graph.reverseClosure sets underApprox to true whenever the queried node itself sources an unresolved edge, even though the returned closure array contains only real resolved node hashes and no null placeholder for the hole.

Unlike the project, task, and pr kinds, which each declare exactly one optional field (grounding or ref), the logbook kind declares an empty OPTIONAL array, so every one of its template keys is required and any logbook write missing one is rejected.

The readRefusal governance check near the top of main() is skipped only when command === 'init'; every other routed command, including read-only ones like query, doctor, node, relations, negations, transitions, verify-fact, and verify-store, is refused before any door opens whenever deps.readRefusal is set.
The test asserts OWN_CAP is pinned to exactly 1500, the token ceiling an OwnPack's tokenEstimate must not exceed.

orientationTokens is tested to return exactly the whitespace-separated word count of the goal string (240 for words(240), 300 for words(300)), so the token cap is enforced as a simple word count rather than an actual tokenizer estimate.

isClosedSlotError recognizes a refusal structurally rather than by class identity: a plain object carrying only a `reason` property equal to CLOSED_SLOT_DISCRIMINANT (no ClosedSlotError instance at all) is accepted as true, simulating what a second module instance's error would look like.

The MCP server's listTools() is asserted to return exactly seven tools in the fixed order [atlas-init, atlas-query, atlas-emit, atlas-reconcile, atlas-link, atlas-relations, atlas-negations], with atlas-link (governance) preceding the two read-only relations/negations tools.

when a leg itself throws a MalformedArgsError, the handler routes it to the same `malformed-args` discriminant used for a schema-level door refusal, even though in this case the leg actually ran, unlike the door-level case where the leg is never invoked.

Every dependency-axis child node produced by build() has a 64-character hex key that is identical to its own subtreeHash, meaning that axis's identity is a content-independent id rather than a hash folded from the node's contents.

defaultBudget's ceiling is not linear in the frontier size: a small frontier (4) yields a ceiling equal to that count, but a large frontier (500) is clamped down to the fixed CEILING_CAP rather than returned as-is.

dependencyClaimParser rejects a DEPENDS-ON line that itself includes a trailing '@ scope' as unparseable (abstains), because scope is always derived from cand.site rather than accepted from the model's answer, so a model that tries to specify its own scope is refused rather than honored.
The `--abstained` flag suppresses ALL grounded-negative lines from the render, not just filters the count, leaving only abstention lines visible.

A symlink that points at a real tracked directory is walked as a leaf carrying only the link text with no children, while the linked directory's own file is still present exactly once under its real path — the walker never mirrors a directory's contents under the link path.

Every test case in this file asserts decision === 'CREATE', including the cases with a duplicate claimNorm at an adjacent anchor, so despite the file being named 'adjacency', none of its cases exercise or pin an UPDATE/merge outcome — the suite only proves that adjacency-based merging never fires anymore.

After a rebase produces a new commit sha, the forge's note stays keyed on the OLD sha rather than being re-pointed: readNote on the old sha still returns the original value while readNote on the new sha returns null.

Only the ./types.js re-export uses the type-only form (`export type *`); every other module in the barrel (portable, respawn, inject, kinds, awareness, orient, rules, template, logbook) is re-exported with a plain value `export *`.

isScope only checks that a value is a non-empty string usable as a lookup key and returns true even for a scope string no policy has ever declared, so it cannot be relied on as an authorization check — that decision lives elsewhere.

scipName only returns a name when the SCIP symbol's descriptor path has exactly one segment after the file-name component (after.length !== 1 yields null), so it matches top-level file-scope declarations but excludes class members or other nested declarations whose descriptor carries an extra container segment.

The test proves that when a later actor raises the governance tier at the same (anchor, slot) node, the served claim contains only the raiser's own assertion and excludes the earlier, lower-tier claim seeded at that address, i.e. the raise replaces rather than merges the claim set.

verifyRelation compares endpointA/endpointB to reverseCallers/definesAt paths only after stripping everything from the first '::' onward via docOf, so an endpoint carrying a '::symbol' structural refinement still matches a bare file path returned by pathOfHash.

closureInterfaceUnchanged compares the pinned and current closures by counting key occurrences into a Map rather than by per-member lookup, specifically because a length-plus-lookup comparison would misread a swap like pinned [A,A] vs current [A,B] as unchanged when a node key repeats.

The off-surface fallback schema (SCHEMA_OFF_SURFACE, exercised via 'atlas-delete' as Tool) deliberately declares no `properties` and no closed set, so a leg wired under a tool token outside the five governance tools still receives arbitrary arguments unfiltered rather than being refused by additionalProperties:false.

the test's stand-in for the model always returns the exact same fixed claim text regardless of which site is visited, because `echo` is configured with one hard-coded argument shared across every propose invocation rather than being parameterized per site.
keyOf computes the same nodeKey for two facts anchored at the same path even when their scope, claimNorm, and gen fields all differ, so the node identity is independent of those fields.
query output orders multiple grounded nodes by nodeKey rather than by emission/creation order: the bar.ts node, emitted after the foo.ts node, is asserted to render before it.

ratifyCtxFor uses conditional spreads for derivedTier and origin, so calling it with both arguments undefined returns an object with neither key present at all (not present-but-undefined), leaving it structurally identical to the bare DOOR_RATIFY_CTX constant.

The test demonstrates that an own-family-only lookahead fix is order-dependent while the shipped union lookahead is not: applying the github-then-slack regex pair to 'xoxb-AAAAAAghp_BBBBBB' fully redacts both tokens, but applying slack-then-github on the same input leaves '[REDACTED]_BBBBBB' with the second body exposed.

Unlike the resolveAnchorAt teeth case, which re-asserts exitCode for both the real and mutant runs, the reDerives teeth case never asserts drift count or exitCode for its mutant run — only the mechanical/semantic array contents are checked.

Passing an empty frontier object ({ frontier: {} }, with provableFirst unset) produces byte-identical output to omitting the frontier option entirely, so the reorder is gated specifically on provableFirst being present, not on the frontier key itself being supplied.

The test strips `//` line-comments from bin.ts's source before searching for `await initAst()` and `composeRuntime(`, specifically to avoid a false positive from prose in the module header that names both calls before either appears as real code.
Only ./types.js is re-exported with the type-only form (`export type *`); all fourteen other runtime modules listed in this barrel are re-exported with a plain value `export *`.

DOOR-KIND-1 asserts the rejected reason does NOT match /ungrounded/, /unauthorized/, or /unratified/, so the test specifically pins that the kind-contradicting payload is refused by the kind-consistency check itself rather than incidentally by one of those other neighboring gates.

mintSpan and readSpan hash the entire bytes buffer passed in (encoder.hash(bytes)), not just the [start, end) slice, so verifying a span requires presenting the whole original byte content, not merely the cited fragment.

The test asserts a negative regex on the exact two-space indent (/^\s{2}scope: /m) to guard specifically against an unnested top-level 'scope:' line, meaning the render's correctness here hinges on indentation depth, not just on which scope values appear anywhere in the output.

SCN-TOOLS-6e-4 shows createProjectionQueryIndex called with no drift-oracle function wired still returns freshness DRIFTED for a fact whose stored freshness field is FRESH, i.e. the read path fails closed to DRIFTED rather than falling back to trusting the stored value.

hasRequiredFields checks only claimText, claimNorm, provenance, and grounding, even though the exported RequiredAdvisoryField type also lists 'owner' and 'scope' and 'predicateSlot' as required fields — those three are never checked by this function.

the Territory interface types `owner` as a bare `string` and `globs` as `readonly string[]`, so nothing in this type itself restricts owner values to real seat ids or globs values to valid glob patterns.

The count grammar accepts exactly one token after the COUNT: prefix — any trailing text, including a scope annotation like ' @ src' or a numeric literal, makes the whole line unparseable rather than being parsed as extra metadata.

put's error path returns the EMPTY sentinel key directly without ever calling cas.set, so a malformed object is never inserted into the map at all and get(EMPTY) will always return undefined no matter how many malformed puts occur.

loadModelConfig refuses a config whose `args` field is given as a single space-joined string rather than an array, with the error message explicitly stating there is no shell to split it, because the command is executed directly without shell argument splitting.

labelOf and readGoal both silently project malformed or absent payloads to the empty string rather than throwing, so an Orientation channel with a corrupted event payload degrades to a blank line instead of surfacing an error.

The N=2 settle counter advances not only on repeated navigation to the same scope but also on a suppressed (non-navigating) call like Grep or Bash, as long as a scope is already current — so a poke can fire after one navigate plus one unrelated suppressed call, not only after two navigations to the same file.

ToolData (the union carried on Verdict.data via HandlerApi.handle) omits DoctorOut and DiffOut, even though both are defined result types in this same file, so those two tool results cannot flow back through the one handler's Verdict<ToolData> return type.
soleHomeViolations flags a datum only when its entire home set is exactly {pr-attachment}; a datum whose homes include pr-attachment alongside store still passes unflagged.

The fixture writes .atlas/projection.json to disk unconditionally in both the RED and CONTROL cases; only whether it is additionally `git add`-ed and committed differs, so the 'untrusted' refusal in the RED case is triggered purely by the file being git-tracked, not by its mere presence on disk.

PULL_LADDER orders 'cli' as the LAST tier (the floor, tried only after sdk-mcp, registered-mcp, poke-as-file, and relay all fail), not the first-tried tier, and the test explicitly pins this ordering rather than just checking membership.

minePass never rejects its returned promise: a spawn or parse failure (no @@...@@ marker found in stdout) resolves with a PassReport carrying complete:false and a crashed message built from stderr/stdout, rather than throwing or rejecting.
The whole S22 describe block is wrapped in describe.skipIf(!HAVE_DEV_ZERO), so on any platform where /dev/zero does not exist (e.g. Windows) the entire suite is skipped rather than run or failed.

relationsOf only attaches the `seal` property to a RelationEdge when the projection row's `seal` is a string; an unsealed relation row produces an edge object with the `seal` key omitted entirely rather than set to undefined or fabricated as 'proven'.

A caller located outside the negation's scope S (e.g. src/other.ts calling the target while the scope is src/pay) does not block admission of the negation, because the underScope containment check restricts which callers count as refuting witnesses.

a retraction is rendered by the CLI as `retracted: <a> ≢ <b>`, a distinct line and symbol from the `linked:` output used for assertions, so a human reading stdout cannot mistake a withdrawal for a new assertion.
init's skeleton territory view has no invariants property at all (Reflect.get returns undefined), not an empty array, so callers must check for the property's absence rather than its length.

The startup IIFE is invoked with `void` and has no try/catch or .catch handler, so a rejection from initAst, composeRuntime, or server.start becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than a caught, reported startup error.

Running promote a second time over the same still-staged, already-promoted row reports promoted:1 again rather than 0, because there is no marker tracking which staged rows were already promoted in a prior invocation — each call re-presents and re-ratifies the same staged candidates.

localDefs is rebuilt fresh for every document in the outer loop rather than accumulated globally, so a local-symbol definition in one document never suppresses the opaque-ref classification of a same-named local reference in a different document.

commitRefusalOf recognizes its two caught error kinds by two different mechanisms in the same function — `instanceof UnaddressableCasObjectError` for the first, but the structural predicate `isClosedSlotError` for the second — rather than using one consistent recognition strategy.
crossesThreshold uses a strict greater-than comparison (rateOf(territory) > threshold), so a territory whose off-atlas rate is exactly equal to the threshold does NOT trigger the calibration prompt.
route treats an absent origin field identically to an explicit origin:'authored', producing the exact same routing decision for the same candidate and context in every case tested.

readCommit's null check `trailer === null && note === null` only short-circuits when BOTH are absent, but deserializeDossier itself returns null whenever trailerText is null regardless of the note argument — so a commit with a note but no trailer still yields null, silently discarding the note's metering/knowledgeDelta overlay.

unlinkSameAs never removes the peer from a node's sameAs array — it only appends to sameAsRetracted alongside the untouched sameAs list, so after a retraction the node still names the peer in sameAs even though it is now also recorded as retracted.

resolveMergeBase refuses any rev string starting with '-' before ever calling git, so that git cannot misread the revision as a command-line option (a check that costs nothing since no valid sha or refname begins with a dash).

casSnapshot's readdirSync call is invoked with only {recursive: true} (no withFileTypes), so it already returns string[]; the subsequent .filter((n) => typeof n === 'string') is therefore a no-op against that call's actual return type.

reorder() reverses ALL object keys including the SIDE_INDEX names (grounding/status/freshness) that hasNfcKeyCollision deliberately excludes, so the two helper functions do not share the same key-filtering logic even though they operate on the same generated values.

The CAP-WINS test shows the advisory packer fills strictly in input order and stops permanently once the cap is hit: a large row placed before a tiny row that would still fit under the cap is excluded anyway, rather than the packer backfilling with the smaller item that fits (best-fit behavior).

The canonical Pack preimage golden (G_PACK_CANONICAL) omits the `freshness` field from each invariant entirely, so materializePoke's on-disk bytes carry the invariant/advisory bands but not the per-row freshness verdict.

the `doctor hotset` command's exit code depends on whether a doctorSource is injected into main: it is 0 when doctorSource is present, but a non-zero code when it is absent, even though both calls target the same read-only command.
The opts.exact flag in VerifyFactOpts is only read when kind is 'count'; for dependency, definition, and negation requests it is silently ignored regardless of what the caller passes.

When a new file enters the negated scope and drifts the directory's Merkle hash, the negation record's identity survives: the read still returns exactly one line for the same target/scope pair (now marked DRIFTED) rather than orphaning the old record or duplicating a new one.

When two different cross-unit dependency symbols share the same terminal name within one unit, crossUnitDepMap picks between them using plain JavaScript string less-than comparison on the full resolved symbol string, not any locale-aware or semantic ordering.
The frontier is ordered churn-descending then path-ascending, so among files tied on churn the tie is broken lexically by qualifiedPath, as pinned by the fileB.ts-before-fileC.ts expectation.

The tier filter treats a whitespace-padded ' T0' and a lowercase 't0' as poison values to be dropped rather than normalizing/accepting them as T0, so the comparison is exact-string, not trimmed or case-insensitive.

The test pins MAX_SEAM_CARRY to the exact value 74, so any change to the scrub seam's carry-window sizing that shifts this constant will fail this test even if redaction correctness is otherwise unaffected.

A write request landing on a node that carries no tier field at all bypasses the governance-downgrade/relocation guard entirely, since the reducer can only derive authority from a class the existing resource actually declares.

reasonOf compares only the substring before the first colon in the rejected reason for equality, deliberately avoiding a toContain/substring match, because refusal prose elsewhere in the codebase quotes other refusal-reason constants by name and would otherwise satisfy a substring check spuriously.

resolveProposer('/nonexistent-repo-for-slot-gate', ...) is used to test the throw on an unknown mining arm, proving the arm-name validation happens before any repo path or model config is read, since a nonexistent path is passed without causing a different error.

The third `it` block (MCP door parity) never calls repo.commit itself; it relies on execution order, reusing the HEAD advance performed as a side effect inside the second `it` block, so running it in isolation would not reproduce the behind-HEAD state it asserts on.

Every pinned-golden assertion passes the MIGRATION remediation string as a second argument directly to expect(), not to .toBe(), so the custom failure message is attached at the expect() call rather than at the matcher call.

The TOTAL test distinguishes two kinds of emptiness with different messages: a scope path that names no unit in the code index at all prints 'names no unit in the code index', while a real code unit that exists but has nothing filed under it prints 'NO fact is filed under it yet' and still shows its terrain.

SCN-ADAPTER-8c's guarantee that ranking mints no fact is verified structurally by reading git-history.ts's own source and asserting its import lines contain no match for /knowledge|store|upsert/i, rather than by a runtime write-spy.

SCN-KERNEL-7a-1 creates one store and one log instance and reuses them across all 500 fast-check runs, whereas the separate PROP-KERNEL-7 test creates a fresh store and log inside the property function on every single run.
Adding, changing, or removing a GroundingEntry's span field leaves the fact's id bit-identical, because the canonical preimage used for hashing does not include the span.

RawTerritory is typed as Omit<Territory, 'tier'>, so the guarantee that the structural walk can never hand init() a tier above T2 is enforced by the type system itself (there is no tier field to read from raw at all), not merely by runtime discipline in createInit's mapping.

createSkeletonSource takes an injectable revIndex option, and when the rev argument matches the resolved HEAD sha it takes a different working-tree code path (reading the SCIP dump) than when the rev is any other value (which routes through the injected revIndex.axesAt instead).

readScipFromBytes derives the definition/reference role by bitwise-ANDing symbolRoles against 1 rather than checking equality, so any symbolRoles value with that low bit set (not just the exact Definition constant) is classified as a definition.

The Encoder interface's hash() method is typed to return only Hash, so nothing in this file provides a typed way to produce a SubtreeHash or NodeKey value through Encoder — those two brands must be minted by some other mechanism not declared here.

The skeleton memo key joins repo and rev with a literal NUL byte, not the two-character backslash-zero escape, because a repo path could legally contain the latter and would break injectivity of the join.

store.put returns the empty string (not a hash digest, and never throws) for an object whose keys NFC-collide, and store.get('') then returns undefined, so such an object is rejected without ever being retrievable under any key.

SCN-KERNEL-2a-1 enforces the single-digest-seam invariant not through runtime behavior alone but by reading the raw source text of canonical.ts and index.ts off disk at test time and regex-matching for the literal strings blake3/sha256/createHash, failing if either file imports a digest primitive directly.

rank()'s returned order keeps a nested unit (the arrow-function closure inside greet) immediately after its parent function and ahead of a sibling top-level unit (privateHelper), even though the closure itself carries no exported flag — nesting groups a unit with its parent rather than a flat exported-then-unexported sort applied uniformly across all units.

The log() helper keys its Map by each event's id field (not contentHash or nodeKey), so two events sharing the same id in the same array would silently collide and the later one would overwrite the earlier one in the resulting EventLog.

nfcCollision's two assignments to o['café'] do not overwrite each other despite the identical source spelling, because the two string literals are different Unicode byte sequences (precomposed vs. combining accent), so the resulting object genuinely carries two distinct keys.

A decision whose decide function returns { next: undefined } (a refusal) settles without ever writing a generation file, verified by readSidecarSet returning an undefined projection afterward — the commit protocol short-circuits before any publish for a no-op decision.

guarded.commitProjection returns a structured {settled:false, refusal:'untrusted'} object for a provenance-refused write, while guarded.persistProjection instead throws an error whose message matches /TRACKED BY GIT/, so the two write paths signal the same refusal through different mechanisms.

createRevIndex is invoked exactly once in this suite, after the v2 commit is made, and the resulting revIndex instance is reused across every drift/plan/lineage assertion rather than being rebuilt per test.
isScope validates only that its input is a non-empty string; it returns true even for a scope name that no policy has ever declared, so it carries no authorization information on its own.

The listTools() assertion checks the tool names with toEqual against a fixed ADVERTISED_TOOLS array, so the exact ORDER the MCP server advertises its seven tools in is pinned, not just their membership.

parseProposals scans the model's reply for JSON-array-shaped substrings from the LAST match backward, and only falls back to an earlier match if a later one fails to parse or parses into zero usable {target,verdict} entries, rather than always taking the very last array in the text.

The test uses a gate whose emit() throws unconditionally, so runExtract must never even call the gate when the proposer returns an { abstain } result — the malformed-answer path is proven to short-circuit before reaching admission, not merely to produce zero facts.

The dv and fv variables in the second drift test are computed by calling cas.checkDrift with literally identical arguments (oracle, grounding, after) — neither call references hDoc or hFact — so the `dv).toBe(fv)` assertion commented as "byte-identical routing across kinds" is trivially true rather than actually comparing the Doc's and the Fact's drift routing.

When a grounding mixes a directory-level file anchor and a symbol anchor (e.g. [file('src'), sym('src/a.ts::1:fn:f')]), the primaryAnchorId resolves to the symbol's qualifiedPath, not the file's, so a coarser file-level anchor present alongside a symbol anchor does not become or dilute the primary anchor.

makeFixtureRepo writes a .gitignore excluding .atlas/* except policy.json and index.scip, so the durable store atlas emit writes is deliberately left untracked while the SCIP dump and policy stay committed.

runDoctor is called for the `index` subcommand with its DoctorSource argument set to `undefined` and a third callback argument (`() => reportIndexPlan(repoPath!)`) supplied instead, showing that runDoctor accepts a distinct third parameter to serve `index` without requiring a DoctorSource at all.

readAfterBareClone checks the trailer for the key first and returns immediately if found, so if the same key exists in both the trailer and the note the trailer's value always wins and the note is never even consulted.

The off-seam digest gate (SCN-KERNEL-2a-2) calls readdirSync(dir) without a recursive option, so it only scans top-level files directly under src/ and would miss a vendored digest placed in any subdirectory of src/.

relationKey hashes the endpoints in the order supplied without sorting them, so swapping a and b (with the same kind) produces a different NodeKey rather than colliding into the same relation identity.

lineMerge resolves an id collision between the two branches by first-seen-wins: it concatenates ours' parsed events before theirs' and only inserts an id into the map when absent, so if both sides carry an event with the same id, ours' copy is kept and theirs' is silently discarded.
The final test asserts all four captured SHAs (mb, mainTip, topicTip, cGreet) are pairwise distinct, while separately asserting r0 equals mainTip exactly rather than being a fifth distinct value.

the counter-keyed-line teeth constructs its malformed event by spreading an already-valid Event and overwriting only its `id` field with a literal string, so isContentKeyed is shown to detect a corrupted id without any other field of the event needing to change.
Building the same tree produces an identical subtreeHash for the territory root and the spatial root, because the axis name is not part of the node fold's hash preimage.

The Status union mixes casing conventions: three of its four literal members ('HOLDS', 'BROKEN', 'NA') are uppercase while the fourth ('advisory') is lowercase, so a caller cannot pattern-match all Status values with a single case-normalization assumption.

createAttach's attach() checks the returned hash with strict equality against the specific empty-string sentinel (hash === ''), not a general falsy/truthy check, so any other hash value the injected store might return - even an unusual but non-empty one - is accepted without being second-guessed.

Even when --accept-reground is true, a mechanical fact is still surfaced in out.mechanical whether or not it was actually accepted for re-grounding, so regroundedCount alone (not membership in out.mechanical) distinguishes accepted from merely-classified-mechanical.

makeFrecencyApi's rank() uses each entry's full `rule` text as the RuleRecord id, so two ProjectMemoryEntry objects with identical rule text but different scopes would be treated as the same record identity in the ranking/eviction ledger lookups.

runLeg is typed and hardcoded to take a Fix (with factA/factB), so it cannot be called with the RenameFix or DupFix fixtures this same file also builds, even though all three exist to feed the same reconcile leg the file documents.
sourceKey uses the facet's own first grounding anchor's subtreeHash as its cache key when one exists, and falls back to hashing the whole entry only when the facet has no grounding anchor at all.

DiskStore's commitStaging and commitProjection methods share an identical enough type signature that the test can reassign `commitStaging: (d) => real.commitProjection(d)` on an object typed as DiskStore without any cast, meaning nothing in the store's own interface types distinguishes a staging commit from a projection commit.

walkFileTree silently skips a git-tracked file that has been deleted from the working tree (readFileSync ENOENT is swallowed) rather than throwing or aborting the whole walk, while its readable sibling files still appear in the result.

createTransport's resolve() implementation takes its seat and need parameters as _seat/_need (unused), so the returned Resolution never actually varies with the seat identity or the requested scope — only harness.canPropagateMcp affects the result.

hasWhyNot treats an empty string whyNot the same as a missing one (both fail the length>0 check), so the SCN-KNOW-13b-2 fixture's whyNot: '' is not a valid why-not and correctly still trips the violation.

The F1 test constructs a fixture where node-identity keys (nk-*) and content subtreeHashes (st-*) are deliberately distinct and the hub's subtreeHash is chosen to sort alphabetically LAST, specifically to prove rank() still places the most-referenced node first rather than burying it via an alphabetical tie-break bug.

reconcile assigns an owner even to a territory that the manifest's territories list omits entirely (only 'docs' is listed, yet 'http' still resolves an owner from blame), so manifest listing is not a precondition for ownership resolution.

ClaimEntry is declared as a bare type alias of Event (`export type ClaimEntry = Event`), not as its own interface, so code using ClaimEntry and code using Event operate on the identical type rather than two merely structurally-compatible ones.
makeRunController's genesis() does not throw even when the injected plan() function itself throws synchronously, not just when visit() fails per-site.
The byte-identity assertion only compares stdout and exitCode between the two runMine calls, so any other field the returned result object might carry is not checked for equality by this test.

SCN-TOOLS-15a-1 tests append-only behavior specifically by attempting to reuse an EXISTING row's key with different value bytes (not a fresh forged key), confirming the same id(value)===key grounding check that refuses back-channel writes also blocks an attempted in-place overwrite of a prior row.
`atlas init` is asserted as the one command exempt from the untrusted-store refusal even when staging is tracked in git, so it still exits 0 over a repo whose every other command refuses.

Three distinct constants — REJECTED_UNAUTHORIZED, REJECTED_UNAUTHORIZED_ANCHOR, and REJECTED_UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET — all begin with the word "unauthorized" but have three different discriminant prefixes before their first colon ("unauthorized", "unauthorized for anchor", "unauthorized for target"), so equality-on-discriminant matching can distinguish them even though a substring check on "unauthorized" could not.

The 'index' subcommand is dispatched and can succeed even when no DoctorSource is wired at all, because its check-and-return happens before the `if (!source)` guard, so 'atlas doctor index' works independently of whether the read-only durable-store source was ever composed.
validateTemplate accepts any non-null, non-array object as a valid template regardless of which fields it contains — it performs no check for a required field set or a per-field cap.

makeRunController tracks at most one in-flight run in a single closure variable `pending`, and calling `genesis()` again unconditionally overwrites it, so starting a second genesis run before resuming the first silently discards the first run's resume checkpoint with no guard or error.

readSpan is refused even when the span's contentHash is swapped for a genuine digest minted from a completely different, unrelated file's bytes, showing the check compares the digest against the presented bytes rather than merely verifying the digest is well-formed or was legitimately produced by mintSpan.

SCN-GL-9's link over an endpoint carrying an unrecognized tier value ('T3', outside the known tier set) is refused for a plain 'lead' ratifier but succeeds for 'billy', showing an unrecognized/garbage tier value is treated as the strictest class rather than ignored or defaulted permissively.

The exhaustive law in SCN-GROUND-4-1 shows gateHolds requires freshness to be exactly FRESH to serve HOLDS: both DRIFTED and STALE downgrade to NA identically, even though the surrounding narrative only calls out drifted grounding.

sealProbe treats an explicitly present but empty-string whyNot the same as a missing one: { whyNot: '' } still records violation:true, so a caller that sets whyNot to '' to signal 'checked, nothing to report' is indistinguishable from never having set it at all.

isSemanticSlot is re-exported as a named VALUE export on its own line, placed before the `export type * from './types.js'` star, specifically so the star's type-only degradation does not demote this one value binding to a type-only reference.

buildRetrievalModel's anchor-to-content-hash bridge appends every fact's contentHash to a per-anchor bucket rather than overwriting it, so a single anchor path backing multiple grounded facts contributes all of them to blastRadius, not just the most recently processed one.
Editing only the text inside the template's HTML justification comment changes createPromptFactory's digest even though the built prompt text sent to the model stays byte-identical.

isGrounded uses a strict typeof-string check on subtreeHash rather than coercing it to a string first, so a value like undefined or null (which would stringify to a non-empty string) is correctly rejected as not grounded instead of fail-open passing.

The fixture exercises a DOUBLE cast (`asOperand as unknown as Foo`), not just a single `as`, and still asserts the operand is classified ESCAPE, so the escape classifier's as-expression rule is pinned to hold even when the value is chained through two casts.

negationFact() uses a conditional spread to OMIT the authzScope property entirely when opts.authzScope is undefined, rather than setting the key to an explicit undefined value, so the pre-split fixture objects have no `authzScope` key at all (not merely a falsy one).

The SIDE_INDEX key filter is applied inside the recursive serialize() call itself, so a nested object anywhere in the tree that happens to have a 'grounding', 'status', or 'freshness' key gets that key stripped too, not only the top-level CasObject's own fields.
A tracked file whose language has no configured indexer at all (like a markdown file) produces neither a planned-language line nor an honest-hole line in the doctor output — it is simply omitted.

reconcile's mechanical/semantic split is order-independent: the test deliberately interleaves mechanical and semantic drifted facts in `all9` (m1,s1,m2,s2,...) rather than grouping them, and the split still comes back correctly partitioned and covering all nine ids.

The groundable check `o.admitted || !o.anchorFailed` relies on short-circuit evaluation: when o.admitted is true the right-hand `o.anchorFailed` access is never reached, which is necessary because the Outcome union only carries an anchorFailed field on the admitted:false branch.

createMine's onSeedsDropped observer fires exactly once per mine() pass (dropped equals [1], not [1,1]) even though the test reads both the mined candidate list and its qualifiedPaths afterward, confirming the structural fallback frontier is built once per pass rather than recomputed separately for seeds vs. candidates.

listGenerations sorts primarily by generation number descending, but when two on-disk filenames parse to the same number it breaks the tie by placing the lexicographically SMALLER filename first, the opposite direction from the primary sort.

The operator emit door's seal-stripping is value-agnostic: it strips a forged seal:'proven' (SCN-GE-3-seal) and equally strips a forged seal:'justified' (A1-forgery) from the durable row, and an authored UPDATE over a previously-promoted node also drops the incumbent's proven seal rather than inheriting it through the reducer's spread of prior fields.

filePathOf resolves the file portion of a qualifiedPath by splitting at the FIRST '::' occurrence, so a qualifiedPath containing more than one '::' separator would have everything after the first one, including any subsequent '::' segments, treated as part of the discarded suffix rather than the file path.

The commit-refusal ternary at the end of emit() only explicitly discriminates 'contended' and 'untrusted'; any other committed.refusal value (including a value the CommitRefusal type does not name) falls through to REJECTED_UNREADABLE_STORE by default.

atLeast values of 0 and -1 are rejected by the same malformed-input check as 1.5, NaN, and Infinity, so the count gate treats any non-positive integer as malformed exactly like a non-integer, and in every case the oracle is never consulted.

deriveSubsumes never explicitly excludes a node paired with itself; self-pairs are eliminated only as a side effect of requiring the broader anchor's segment count to be strictly less than the narrower's.

relationsOf is strictly directional and not auto-mirrored: querying the subject endpoint with direction 'in' or the object endpoint with direction 'out' both return zero edges, even though the same edge resolves correctly for the matching directions.

spawnRecall throws an Error rather than returning an empty or default ClosingFold when the archive has no fold matching both the requesting seat as owner and the exact resumed unit kind+id, so a re-spawn onto an unrecognized unit fails loudly instead of silently starting with blank retry context.

A relation nodeKey hit routes to UPDATE (set-union of claims) rather than SUPERSEDE, unlike a predicate nodeKey hit with a differing check which routes to SUPERSEDE, because a relation carries no `check` field to compare.

hits.decay re-reads the served set live on each call rather than snapshotting it once at bindHits construction: the test mutates the pack via p.set([Q]) between two decay() calls and the second call's result reflects that later mutation.

SCN-SA-4 shows sameAsClassOf can merge two live nodes (kA, kB) into one governance class even though neither names the other and deriveSameAs finds no relation between them at all — the bridge is solely a shared non-current peer key (kRETIRED) that each names independently.

resolveProposer's modelIdentity never contains a fabricated version number: when the --version probe cannot be read (e.g. a nonexistent binary), the identity string explicitly says the probe failed instead of inventing a version.

createGovernedStore's write() returns the same admitted:true verdict whether the row's key was newly inserted into the medium or already present (in which case the Map.set is skipped entirely), so the caller cannot distinguish a fresh write from a no-op re-emit from the verdict alone.

Unlike the invariants/gotchas/manifest loops above it, which keep trying later (possibly smaller) candidates after one fails to fit, the advisory band's fill loop sets a permanent advisoryCapped flag on the first miss and skips every subsequent candidate regardless of whether it would individually fit.

the relocation gate check `node.scope !== stored.scope` compares the incoming write's declared scope against `stored.scope` (the CAS bytes), not against `rowScope`/`authorityScope`, so relocation is checked against the authenticated bytes even on the carrier-less legacy row path where authority itself was derived from those same bytes.

The back-compat test strips derivedAt from every row of every file on disk whose name starts with 'projection' and ends with '.json', not just the single mirror file, so the durable store can be spread across multiple physical files that all must be downgraded together.

packToolName derives the pack name from only the LAST path segment (e.g. 'file:billing/charge' -> 'own_charge', 'file:billing/refund' -> 'own_refund'), discarding the directory prefix rather than encoding the full scope path.

pullOptimize falls back to the push materialize() path whenever opts.pull is undefined, even if harness.nativePull reports 'available' — both conditions in the ternary must hold for the native pull port to actually be invoked.

the read-only guarantee on the diff handle is verified by asserting five specific method names (write, apply, applyInto, set, put) are all undefined on the returned object at runtime, rather than by any type-level check.

relationWitnessTrusted requires the witness's relationKind to equal both the literal string 'depends-on' AND the relation node's own relationKind field, so it also rejects a witness claiming depends-on when the node itself declares a different relationKind.

Within signalsMemo, the `messages` array is left in raw git-log order and never sorted, while the sibling `owners` and `coChanged` arrays computed in the same function are explicitly sorted with byPath, so signals() mixes a sorted and an unsorted list in the same returned object.

negationKey hashes a canonical object with the field names neg/t/s (not the relationKind/target/scope names themselves), so the preimage's own key set is what keeps it from colliding with any other hash that happened to canonicalize the same three values under different field labels.

The union of arms is keyed by fact id in a Map before classification, so if two arms happened to seed facts sharing the same id, only one would survive into the final advisory/dependency/count split rather than both being counted.

The barrel re-exports types.js with the type-only `export type *` form while every runtime module (relate/pack/own/poke/drop/ledger/offatlas) uses the value form `export *`, so types.ts is the only re-export guaranteed to contribute zero runtime code to the bundle.

createTranscriptStore's put() calls scrub(body) fresh on each invocation with no carried state between calls (no seam buffer in the closure), so a credential whose bytes are split across two separate put() calls on the same logical transcript is not redacted, since neither call alone sees the full credential.
The advertised GOVERNANCE_SURFACE has exactly five tool names, with the governed atlas-link door asserted as the fifth advertised tool alongside init/query/emit/reconcile.

writeCommit throws an Error instead of writing anything if the given `sha` is not the repository's current HEAD, so it can only attach a trailer to the tip commit and cannot amend an arbitrary historical commit.
The 'untrusted' staging-refusal text instructs the operator to run `git rm --cached -r .atlas` and add `.atlas/*` to `.gitignore` as the remedy, rather than simply saying the store is git-tracked.

The stand-in model process is made to echo a markdown-fenced 'atlas-fact' code block containing a JSON object with a claim key, rather than raw claim text, so the pipeline under test parses proposals out of that fenced-JSON wrapper format.

In this suite, dropping a fact's symbol anchor and grounding it only at a file changes its computed nodeKey even when slot and claim text stay identical, because primaryAnchorId falls back to the first grounding entry's path (the file) when no symbol anchor is present.

renderData renders an InvRow's missing freshness field as the literal string '?' rather than defaulting to 'FRESH', because rendering an absent verdict as FRESH would falsely read as a verification that had actually happened.
