makeGitSbx never checks out 'main' after branching except to write the shared service.py bump (SERVICE_X), so main's src/util.ts is never rewritten past the mb commit and stays at greet's original body.

commonSegmentPrefix returns the empty string both when it is given zero paths and when the given paths diverge already at their first segment, so an empty-string result alone cannot distinguish 'no callers at all' from 'callers whose common scope is the whole repo'.

When the current sidecar generation file is corrupt and readSidecarSet falls back to an older generation, it reports that older generation's own identity verdict rather than treating the corrupt head as unstamped or current.
The test helper logOf keeps only the FIRST event when two supplied events share the same id, silently discarding any later ones with the same id rather than overwriting or merging them.

makeFixScip encodes a 'reference' occurrence not with a named SymbolRole constant but with the bare literal `symbolRoles: 0`, while a 'definition' occurrence uses the named `SymbolRole.Definition` constant, so reference-ness is represented as the protobuf field's zero/absent value rather than an explicit role.

For the dependency arm the harness stores a synthesized claimNorm sentence that always describes a REFERENCE ('references'), never the word 'calls', even though the model's own proposal claimed the opposite relationship.

SCHEMA_OFF_SURFACE is the only schema in this module that omits `additionalProperties: false` — every one of the five real SCHEMAS entries sets it, but the off-surface fallback only declares `type: 'object'` with no property closure at all.

The scope checked for unresolved edges includes the origin node itself (not just its reverse-closure members), so a node with zero dependents but its own unresolved outgoing edge still flags underApprox:true and pulls in its coChanged band, even though the origin is excluded from the returned closure array.

Unlike every other module in this barrel which is re-exported with `export *`, source.js is re-exported by naming only its specific runtime functions and the PortableSource/SourceApi types, so its Home/Placement/Source model stays unexported.

The reinvoke module's exported surface, checked via Object.keys(reinvoke), consists of exactly redispatch and replay — no member whose name matches /resume|continuefrom|resumeat|continue_from|resume_at/i exists on it.

Explicitly passing origin:'authored' to ratifyCtxFor routes the mined candidate identically (auto-accept) to passing no origin argument at all, so the two are pinned as equivalent rather than 'authored' being treated as some third distinct origin state.

childName falls back to the child's FULL key (not a relative name) whenever the child's key does not start with the parent's key, so a node whose id scheme does not literally prefix its children's keys with its own key folds those children under their absolute key rather than a short relative name.

Unlike every other module in this barrel, which is re-exported with a wildcard `export *`, brand.js is re-exported through an explicit named list of exactly three bindings (asHash, asSubtreeHash, asNodeKey).

For the same 3-file fixture, the dependency and count arms mark opposite files as provable: consumer.ts is provable under dependency but not count, while lib.ts is provable under count but not dependency, so switching ATLAS_MINE_SLOT changes which sites the reorder favors rather than merely widening or narrowing the same set.

The negation-seed test asserts the admitted negation candidate's grounding.entries array has length 0 at admit time, meaning the gate mints the negation's identity and target/scope before any grounding entries are attached to it.

generatedOwner takes a `graph` parameter but immediately discards it with `void graph`, so the owner it computes depends only on the blame tally and is completely unaffected by the structural depends-on graph passed in.

when callTool is invoked for RELATIONS_TOOL with no leg argument at all, it falls straight through to the injected fakeHandler rather than being specially intercepted, so its error text is the handler's generic 'off-surface' rejection rather than any relations-specific message.

The blameCalls helper filters the git spy's recorded calls down to only those whose second argument array contains 'blame', so the subprocess count assertions ignore any other memoized git commands invoked during the same test.

The financeIndex test double resolves territory by splitting the scope on '/' and checking for an exact path-segment match against 'finance', so a scope containing 'finance' only as a substring of a longer segment (e.g. 'nonfinance') would fall through to the 'root/' territory rather than matching.

IDENT_RE matches any bare identifier token by name, so the sibling BFS in createUnitSiblingReader can pull in an unrelated same-file unit merely because its leaf name happens to appear as a substring identifier somewhere in an included unit's text, without verifying it is actually referenced as that symbol.

The antisymmetry check adds Math.sign(compareSiteOrder(a,b)) and Math.sign(compareSiteOrder(b,a)) rather than comparing one to the negation of the other, specifically to avoid a false failure from Math.sign(0) returning +0 while its arithmetic negation would be -0 (values Object.is distinguishes).

When ATLAS_ACTOR is set in the environment it takes priority over the repo's local git user.email even when the two identities are members of different policy scopes, so setting ATLAS_ACTOR always silences whatever git config the repo carries rather than the two being merged or git winning as the more specific source.

When a proposer's claim carries no rawAnswer, the returned proposal object omits the rawAnswer field entirely rather than setting it to undefined, verified via not.toHaveProperty rather than a value check.

predicateWith builds its payload as an untyped `raw` object and forces it to GroundedFact via a double cast (`as unknown as GroundedFact`), so every malformed `check` shape in this file's test cases bypasses TypeScript's structural checking entirely rather than being narrowed by the GroundedFact union.
When the wp carries no valid string transcriptSha, meter() defaults it to asHash(''), the sealed hash digest of the empty string, rather than a literal empty string or some other sentinel value.

CARRIER-3 pins that changing a fact's scope and tier (core/T2 to other/T0) while keeping the same anchor and claimNorm leaves keyOf() unchanged (the same nodeKey) while the content id() digest differs, confirming scope/tier are excluded from the node-identity preimage but included in the content-address preimage.

The TEETH test does not actually revert assembleHandler and re-run it against the missing path; it instead calls readScip directly on the missing path as a stand-in proof that the unguarded call would throw.

buildProvable's filtered DiskStore uses two separately-built Sets from the same re-proven pairs: `get` is gated on reProvenContentHashes while `loadProjection`'s current-map filter is gated on reProvenNodeKeys, so the CAS-read leg and the projection-read leg are filtered by different keys rather than sharing one membership check.

The second test proves the query result's subsumes list is filtered by the query's own scope even though deriveSubsumes itself would still relate an out-of-scope module/function pair: facts anchored under 'api' produce no subsumes edge and no pack invariant when the query scope is 'src'.

P1 and P2 are constructed with check bodies that differ only in surrounding whitespace (CHECK1 vs CHECK2), and the test asserts P2.id equals P1.id exactly, confirming nodeKey identity is computed from the normalized check rather than the raw expr string.

in case 3, the hand-built store stub implements put, get, persistProjection, loadProjection, commitProjection, and commitStaging but has no upsert method, and the whole object is forced through an `as unknown as MineDeps` cast rather than satisfying the MineDeps type on its own.

The sound-oracle arm's emitted advisory node still carries a 'proven' seal even though it has neither a 'check' nor a 'status' field, so 'seal' is populated independently of whether the node carries a checkable predicate.

verifyDependency never returns a 'refuted' verdict in this suite: every case where no in-scope caller is found or the target/world is problematic resolves to 'abstain' with a specific reason, never a proven-false result.

resolveCurrent only scans src.spatial and src.territory for a matching qualifiedPath; it never scans a src.dependency root, so a grounding anchor whose key exists only in the dependency axis will unconditionally resolve to undefined.

blindTo simulates a partial CAS restore by pruning only specific hashes from `get`, while `put` still writes new objects normally, so a caller can test a store that is missing SOME objects but can still accept fresh writes.

The singular resolveMineSlot's unset default ('advisory') matches exactly the first element of the plural resolveMineSlots' unset default array (['advisory','dependency','count']), so the two independently-tested defaults are consistent with each other rather than diverging.

This file imports reinvoke.ts twice — once by named import (redispatch, replay) and once as a namespace (import * as reinvoke) — specifically so the alias-absence test can enumerate Object.keys(reinvoke) at runtime and catch any additional export the file's own named imports would silently ignore.

When a predicate proposal's slot is type-expressible (soundOracle.expressible returns true) so admit routes through typeOracle.diagnose instead of predicate.synthesize, the resulting admitted fact still comes back as kind:'advisory' with neither a `check` nor a `status` field, even though the input was a PredicateProposal.

The staged predicate's nodeKey is asserted to be slot-sensitive: computing nodeKey over the identical candidate but with slot set to undefined produces a DIFFERENT key than the one actually staged, proving the predicate identity folds in the slot rather than being derivable from anchor+check alone.

coerceStatus recognizes exactly four incoming Status values (HOLDS, BROKEN, NA, advisory), but gateHolds only ever inspects the HOLDS case for downgrade, so an incoming 'advisory' status passes straight through the gate unchanged rather than being evaluated against groundedness or freshness.

In the ceiling-drop test the run's reported budgetSpent equals coverage's seeded+abstained+unrecorded counts summed together, so unvisited (dropped-by-ceiling) sites are excluded from what counts as budget consumed.

isContainedIn resolves the requested path (not just root) through realpathSync before comparing FileIds, so a symlink encountered anywhere along the candidate's ancestor chain is followed to its real target before each dev/ino comparison, not only at the two endpoints.

createQuery's tokenEstimate is computed only from packTokens(governing) + packTokens(advisory) — the surviving, actually-returned rows — deliberately excluding whatever the advisory band's cap dropped, so the estimate always describes the size of the pack the caller received, never the size of the pre-truncation set.

makeFixScipPy creates a brand-new temp directory via mkdtempSync on every call, so calling it twice yields two distinct scipPath values even though the serialized SCIP bytes written are always identical.

firstSplitDisagreement's O(n^2) pairwise-offset sweep only runs when its `pairs` parameter is true, and the adversarial-alphabet test disables it for any generated string longer than 40 characters by passing `s.length <= 40` as that argument.

publish() classifies a generation as 'superseded' rather than 'lost' using the strict inequality headNow < gen + RETAINED_GENERATIONS, so a writer whose name was overtaken by fewer than RETAINED_GENERATIONS newer generations is treated as durably published instead of retried.

Two distinct advisory claims mined at the same site (same anchor+slot) collapse into a single staged row (current.size === 1) because nodeKey is derived from anchor+slot alone and never reads the claim text, so a second differently-worded claim at that site is treated as a re-claim on the existing node, not a new one.

Two of the four declared families (github-token and github-pat) share the identical opening prefix character 'g', so SHAPES_BY_OPENER dispatches to both shapes for that byte and the leftmost scanner must try two regexes at a 'g', not one, unlike the other three families' distinct opening bytes.

modelWired is computed from `deps?.proposer !== undefined || resolved?.wired`, which is always false on the production CLI path for the first disjunct because the resolved proposer is only ever assigned into `d.proposer` via a `??` fallback, never read back from the original `deps` object.

The 'NO BRICK: two symbols in the SAME file' case does not actually use two distinct symbols — its sites array repeats the identical pair ['src/billing.ts','charge'] twice rather than pairing charge with a second, different function in that file.

The 'out' direction result is sorted by relationKind alphabetically ('calls' before 'depends-on'), not by insertion order or by contentHash/nodeKey, since r2 (calls, inserted second) precedes r1 (depends-on, inserted first) in the OUT test's expected order.

The suite's own case-folding probe determines whether the case-variant bypass test runs at all: it creates a directory and checks via statSync's dev/ino whether an uppercased spelling denotes the same directory, then skips the whole test rather than asserting a different outcome on a case-sensitive filesystem.

flowsFromScrub and spreadsIdentifier both cap their const-initializer resolution chain at depth 8 (depth > 8 returns false), so a scrub call reached only through more than eight levels of indirect `const x = y` aliasing would be reported as NOT provably flowing from the scrub, a false negative rather than a false positive.

canonicalise only shrinks an unbounded match's body when the shape declares both no ceiling AND a non-empty filler string; a matched shape lacking a filler is left completely un-canonicalised (its full, unbounded body kept) rather than being skipped in some safer bounded way.

headSha is called at most once per cover() invocation, before the per-node loop, rather than once per row, so the cost of resolving live HEAD is paid a single time regardless of how many current nodes fall under the requested scope.

The concurrent-writer durability test does not assert that all W emit processes succeed; it only requires accepted to be at least 1 and checks that durable node count equals K plus whatever accepted turned out to be, so a run where most writers are rejected by contention still passes.

createNegationLeg's freshness-oracle parameter is optional, and calling it with no second argument at all (not even undefined explicitly) still yields DRIFTED rather than throwing or defaulting to FRESH.

createNegationLeg's freshnessOf helper re-fetches the full fact from CAS by contentHash on every call rather than trusting any cached freshness on the node, and returns DRIFTED both on a CAS miss and whenever resolveFreshness yields anything other than exactly 'FRESH' (including a collapsed STALE).

The empty-frontier and seeded-no-proposer states are distinguished by which env/deps are passed to runMine — passing only NO_MODEL_ENV with default deps yields the empty-frontier message, while additionally injecting skeletonSource/injectedHistory/fakeStore under NO_MODEL_ENV yields the seeded-no-proposer message, so the same env alone does not determine which cause is reported.

archive.supersede's returned `node` is the caller's own `next` object by reference identity (`node === next`), not a fresh object with a supersededBy field mixed in, so the pointer to the prior version lives only in the separate `supersededBy` return value, never on `next` itself.
In the property test, build(k) always maps k to nodeKey `nk-${k % 3}`, so no matter how many integers the generated array contains, the folded state can only ever have up to 3 distinct node buckets.

isPrefix treats two identical segment arrays as a prefix relationship (short === long returns true), so it is a non-strict prefix test that does not distinguish 'is a proper prefix of' from 'is equal to'.

A bare `doctor` with no subcommand produces a distinctly different error message ('requires 1 positional argument') than an unrecognized subcommand does ('unknown doctor subcommand'), showing the CLI's generic positional-arity check runs before doctor's own subcommand-name validation ever executes.

answersDigest is order-independent over the set of stored receipts: feeding answerReceipts in reversed order produces the identical digest and answersStored count as the forward order, so the digest is a function of the set/multiset of receipts, not their sequence.

The 'clean' (fully-resolved) closure in SCN-INDEX-13e-1 still contains C, the same node the coChanged map keys its band on, yet coChanged comes back empty — proving the suppression is gated on the underApprox flag itself, not on whether the coChanged-bearing node is absent from the closure.

planIndexers does not omit unsupported languages from its output plan; an unsupported lang like 'rb' still produces a plan entry, but tagged with tool 'honest-hole' rather than a real indexer name, so callers must check the tool field rather than absence to detect an unindexed language.

Under a sub-frontier budget, which candidates driveMine seeds depends on visiting sites in highest-rank-first order: reversing that order changes the resulting seeded set even though the same sites and budget are used.

bindFreshness narrows a 3-valued grounding-freshness oracle down to only 2 states at the knowledge layer: an oracle that returns the third value 'STALE' is folded into 'DRIFTED' rather than being passed through or causing an error.

driftDetect on a grounding with two entries where one entry's anchor genuinely resolves FRESH in the source but the other entry is empty still returns DRIFTED for the whole grounding, i.e. a single empty leg overrides an otherwise-resolvable sibling leg rather than only that leg being flagged.

auxiliaryStructureCount is computed as backing.size - 1 over a manually-constructed Set that today lists only `axes`; the invariant only catches a future violation if any code that stands up a second structure is also updated to register it in `backing`, so the count is self-reported rather than independently measured.
For a predicate-kind gotcha, ownVerdict renders the claim portion of the row as an empty string rather than stringifying the predicate's check object, avoiding a printed "[object Object]".

strictestTier joins two off-lattice garbage values (e.g. two OFF_LATTICE entries together) to 'T0' rather than to any off-lattice sentinel or garbage-in-garbage-out result, so the join always resolves onto a real class even when neither input was one.

In the UPDATE branch, when a write raises the node to a governing tier (T0/T1) the claims array is replaced with only [req.claimNorm], discarding every prior weaker-tier claim, whereas a same-tier UPDATE unions req.claimNorm into the existing claims array by dedup.

flowsFromRedactor treats a property-access name (the `.name` side of a PropertyAccessExpression, e.g. `from` in `Uint8Array.from(x)`) as unresolvable and skips it during identifier walking, rather than attempting to resolve it against the const-initializer map.

rewriteIndex's local SCIP-building helper marks a defining occurrence with the named `SymbolRole.Definition` constant but marks a referencing occurrence with the bare literal `0` rather than any named role constant.

The S26.4b assertion expect(d).toContain('advisory') is already satisfied by the substring inside 'advisoryDropped', which the preceding assertion in the same test already confirms is present, so it does not independently verify the standalone word 'advisory' appears anywhere in the description.

The durable CAS record for a proven fact carries two distinct fields both named 'scope' at different nesting levels (the top-level authz scope 'atlas:mined' and witness.scope 'src'), and the test explicitly asserts they are unequal so a reader cannot conflate them.

The property-based build() helper deliberately buckets every event's nodeKey to only three possible values (`nk-${k % 3}`) regardless of how large the integer arbitrary's range is, so the fold's resulting node count is asserted to equal the number of distinct k%3 residues actually drawn, never the number of distinct k values.

A child process that exits cleanly (exit 0) after only partially draining a huge stdin write is salvaged to return the stdout it did produce rather than throwing an EPIPE error, but the same salvage is refused when the exit status is non-zero.

The path-traversal test includes an all-uppercase 64-char hex string ('AB' repeated 32 times) as an invalid CAS address purely because of its case, proving the address charset check is case-sensitive to lowercase hex even though the string is otherwise the correct length.

A .tsx file is counted under the 'ts' language bucket rather than its own language row: with one .ts and one .tsx file tracked, reportIndexPlan reports files:2 for lang 'ts' and no separate tsx entry.
The freshness oracle DRIFTS a fact on a whitespace-only reformat inside the cited unit (adding one extra space), because it hashes the unit's raw byte slice rather than normalizing whitespace.

createEmit's return type is narrowed to `{ readonly emit: EmitApi['emit'] }`, not the full EmitApi, so the returned object implements only `emit` and has no `absorb` member at all even though EmitApi declares both.

On a byte-identical DEDUP upsert, a request supplying a DIFFERENT primaryAnchor and slot than the stored node's is entirely ignored — the existing node's anchor/slot are not updated to the new request's values, unlike UPDATE/SUPERSEDE where a supplied request anchor/slot does win.

territories()'s return expression `(atRoot || kids.length > 0 ? kids : [node])` returns kids unconditionally whenever atRoot is true, even when kids is empty (a repository with no top-level territories) — only a NON-root leaf with zero path-children falls back to reporting the node itself.
verifyCount returns 'abstain' rather than throwing or erroring when asked about a symbol that has no definition occurrence in the SCIP output at all.

The UPDATE branch's answerRef handling is asymmetric by presence, not by whether a change occurred: a re-mine that supplies a new answerRef always overwrites the prior one, while a re-mine that omits answerRef entirely (undefined) leaves the prior receipt untouched rather than clearing it.

The suite includes a dedicated ~8000-path-segment test asserting isContainedIn returns a boolean verdict rather than throwing, specifically to guard against a per-segment-recursive implementation blowing the call stack on deep paths.

put() unconditionally throws on the matched-partition branch (kind matches the entry's true partition) rather than returning a MemoryRecord, so the only observable behavior of put in this file is either a KindConflationError or this fixed 'not invented' Error — it never succeeds.

SCN-RETR-10d-1 verifies the absence of a network/model surface not by inspecting relate.ts's runtime behavior but by reading the raw source text of that file at test time and regex-scanning it for forbidden tokens (fetch, await, Promise, openai, anthropic, claude, WebSocket, dynamic import, http(s) URLs).

A fact authored with slot:'rationale' but no explicit tier still renders as an 'inv T1' row and is counted into the invariants/governing band, showing that band membership is decided by tier alone, not by the candidate's slot value.

put explicitly checks typeof bytes !== 'string' after JSON.stringify because JSON.stringify silently returns undefined (rather than throwing) for a bare top-level undefined, function, or symbol, which the catch block alone would not detect.
rank()'s output carries a 1-indexed `rank` field (the hub site gets rank:1, not rank:0), confirmed here by asserting the four-site fixture's ranks equal exactly [1, 2, 3, 4] in descending-PPR order.

unitScopeOf returns the empty string for a top-level unit with no directory separator in its file path, and that empty scope is designed to never match any dependency scope check, so a root-level unit's dependency claim always abstains rather than being granted an over-wide whole-repo scope.

SCN-GE-I9's shifty tier getter deliberately returns the odd sequence T0,T2,T0 (only the second access differs) rather than a simpler two-value alternation, specifically because a naive T0,T2,T2 sequence would trip the downgrade guard on the second read for reasons unrelated to whether tier is snapshotted, making the case pass vacuously.

descentSteps splits each path segment on '::' with no filter for empty tokens, so a stray double-colon (e.g. 'a::::b') produces a step whose token is the empty string, which then fails to match any real child key and causes the whole resolve to miss, rather than being silently collapsed away.
A transcript's git pointer object has exactly two keys, sha and store, and store is always the literal string 'cas' rather than any store-specific identifier.

classifyIdentity compares the stamp to IDENTITY_SCHEMA with strict `===` — no trimming, case-folding, or Unicode normalization — so a stamp that differs only by trailing whitespace or case is classified `foreign` rather than `current`.

queryStale still returns the drifted fact's value (visible) alongside its stale:true flag rather than omitting it from the result; exclusion from the FRESH set only happens when the caller separately filters by the stale flag afterward.

ground() given one resolvable citation and one unresolvable citation produces an entirely EMPTY entries array rather than a one-entry receipt keeping just the resolvable citation — the test asserts g.entries has length 0 even though QP_TAX itself resolves in src, so an unresolvable citation fails the whole fact closed, not just itself.
canonicalForm throws when given a value containing a non-integer floating-point number, rather than serializing it.

spawnRecall returns a fresh copy of the archived fold on every call rather than the same object reference, since two calls with identical arguments compare equal by value (toEqual) but are asserted NOT to be the same reference (not.toBe).

store.supersede leaves the original entry's serialized bytes byte-identical and the store size unchanged at 1, recording the supersession only as a separate append-only link pointer retrievable via store.supersessions(), never by mutating or growing the entries log.

The opaque-vs-hole classification is per-document rather than global: negation-key.ts's collapsed local reference is classified as opaque but excluded from holeSources entirely, so a caller that only inspects holeSources (not opaqueRefSources) would miss this completeness gap.

fill() concatenates the full sorted T0 bucket ahead of the full sorted T1 bucket into one array before walking it with a single running `used` counter and cap check, so every T0 candidate is considered for inclusion before any T1 candidate is, and a large enough T0 set could exhaust the cap and leave the tail entirely T1.

makeDeps's default predicate seam is built by calling predicateSeam() and keeping only its `seam`, discarding the `calls` counters object, so a test using the default deps (no explicit `predicate` override) has no way to inspect how many times synthesize/verify/teeth were invoked.

The visited/budget counter increments after every proposer call regardless of outcome, so a site where the model abstains (returns null or an {abstain} object) still consumes one unit of the budget ceiling just like an admitted site does.
The token cap boundary in injectOrientation is inclusive (<=), so an Orientation whose token count equals exactly ORIENTATION_TOK_CAP (250) is accepted and only 251 or above is rejected.

gateEmitFor's admission decision depends only on the candidate's site id (idOf(c)), never on the content of the proposed seed — it reads seed.claim only to embed it in the fact once admission is already decided, so the fixture's gate would admit a candidate regardless of what the injected proposer claimed.

When verifyDependency returns 'abstain' on a grounded dependency PREDICATE proposal, admit() falls back to a fact of kind 'advisory', not kind 'predicate', so the proposal's own predicate slot is discarded and it lands as a different node kind than what was proposed.
writeWithScanner rejects a scanner whose name is an empty string before ever invoking scan() on the record, so an unnamed scanner never even gets the chance to inspect the record.

The test asserts the three output lines are strictly adjacent in stdout — the cost line must sit at exactly genesis-line-index+1 and the cause line at exactly cost-line-index+1 — so any blank or extra line inserted between them would fail this test even if all three lines' content were otherwise correct.

driftDetect's verdict is invariant to a pure displayLines line-range edit on the grounding entry (the test asserts driftDetect on the original and the shifted-displayLines version return the exact same value), confirming displayLines never participates in the drift decision at all.

this suite detects a reintroduced third parameter on writeDecision/upsert purely by asserting each function's own declared .length (arity), without importing or referencing any config type, so it would catch the parameter coming back even unread and even under a completely different name.

The `::` sub-file refinement token is treated as a full path-separator boundary by resolution, not just `/`, so a character extension immediately after a `::` segment fails to resolve just like one after a `/` segment.

The test reads .atlas/staging.json's 'current' field as an array of [nodeKey, fact] tuples (a serialized Map), not as a plain object keyed by nodeKey, so parsing it with Object.keys or property access would not enumerate the staged facts.

identityAnchorPaths selects the symbol-kind grounding entries for identity whenever at least one exists, and falls back to only the very first entry (regardless of kind) exclusively when zero symbol-kind entries are present, rather than ever mixing symbol and non-symbol entries together.

renderIndexPlan only emits the multi-language clobber note when r.configured.length is strictly greater than 1, so a repository with exactly one configured language plus any number of hole languages never sees the overwrite warning.

the deterministic-sort test seeds nodes in the order (fn, crate, mod) — not in broader-to-narrower order — and still asserts the returned edges come back lexicographically sorted by (broader, narrower), showing deriveSubsumes's output order is independent of the projection Map's insertion/iteration order.

emitFact's `seq` counter is module-level state shared across every call in the test file, so filenames never collide even when the same file calls emitFact against multiple different FixtureRepo instances.

reverseClosure's coChanged band is asserted disjoint from its structural closure set: every member the coChanged band returns is checked to NOT appear in the static closure, so the two are never merged into one presented set.
CEILING_CAP is exactly 200, confirmed by asserting defaultBudget(1000).ceiling equals CEILING_CAP directly rather than a hard-coded literal.

T3b (unknown FIRST endpoint) asserts the stdout contains no 'malformed args' or 'Cannot read properties' text, meaning it positively pins that a specific TypeError-to-caller-blame mislabeling defect does NOT occur, not just that the call exits with a governed refusal code.

ratify() distinguishes an empty-string ratifier token from a non-empty one (by:'' fails, by:'lead' succeeds for a T2 candidate), so the gate checks token non-emptiness generally and only additionally requires the specific token 'billy' for a T0 candidate.

underScope strips the '::' suffix from `anchor` before splitting into segments, but never strips '::' from `scope`, so a scope string that itself contains '::' can never match any anchor, since the anchor side has already had its '::' portion removed before comparison.

In the v2 target-relative branch the phantom-target (target-unresolvable) check runs first, before either scope-closure check; in the fallback blanket branch that same target-unresolvable check runs only after the scope-open check, so the ordering of these two checks differs between the two code paths.

trySoundRelation only calls the `score` obviousness callback after verifyRelation has already returned 'proven', so a witness that fails or abstains verification never has its claim-norm text computed or scored at all.

When the dependency oracle abstains (rather than proving or refuting) on a grounded candidate, the fact is NOT dropped but is instead downgraded to an unsealed advisory fact with predicateSlot undefined — the kind changes from predicate to advisory rather than the fact simply carrying no seal.

coverageLines for an old GenesisReport lacking the coverage field renders exactly one line total, not one line per absent site, and that line reads UNEVALUABLE rather than CLOSES — so the absence is reported as a single verdict, never expanded into fabricated per-site rows.
reverifyVerdict's exit code is binary — computed as rejected ? 2 : 0 — so this function can never itself produce exit code 1.

Scope resolution is case-sensitive: 'srcm0' (lowercase m, matching 'src/m0' if case-folded) is asserted to fail with 'no covering territory' alongside the other non-existent-path variants, so a query differing only in case from a real scope does not resolve.

DOOR-SAMEAS-2 proves a governed link's ratifier requirement is priced over the TRANSITIVE sameAs class (sameAsClassOf) rather than the directly-linked pair: linking B to a third node M is refused for an ordinary ratifier solely because a T0 node A is reachable from B through the earlier signed edge, even though A and M were never directly linked.

SCN-GEN-6a-2 asserts JSON.stringify(loud.facts[0]) does not contain the string '42' even though the candidate's szzBugCommits signal was set to 42, confirming the mined signal score is used for ranking only and never serialized into the emitted Fact.

editDistance's fieldMap folds the ordered `endpoints` pair into a single JSON-stringified field rather than two separate fields, so a relation-direction-reversal mutation that swaps both endpoint positions still counts as an edit distance of exactly 1, not 2.

gateHolds takes the currently-recorded status ('HOLDS') as an explicit first argument rather than deriving it, so the gate's job is to decide whether to KEEP that status or downgrade it to NA, not to compute status from scratch.

isTree only validates that `territories` is an array; it never inspects the shape of individual array elements, so an array containing malformed seeds (missing path/owner/files) still passes the guard and gets mapped through toTerritory unchecked.

readRepoBytes performs no owner-based filtering at all: calling it as a non-owning seat (bob) still returns another seat's (alice's) full memory entries, so owner-scoping is enforced only by injectFor for the turn-header path, not by readRepoBytes itself.

readRefusal and readAdvisory are both spread conditionally into the deps object only when defined, rather than being passed unconditionally, so on a healthy repo those keys are structurally ABSENT from the object rather than present with an undefined value.

byScope collects objects walking the covering chain from the specific node up to its ancestors, but dereferenceSorted then re-sorts everything by raw hash string, so the returned facts carry no trace of the file→module→...→repo roll-up order they were gathered in.

When two events share the same nodeKey and contentHash but differ in a field that IS in the id preimage (like fresh), fold() resolves the collision by picking the event with the lexicographically larger id (MAX-by-id), not the first- or last-arrived event, so the winner is deterministic across delivery orders but is NOT a first-write-wins or last-write-wins rule.

assign's declaration-order tiebreak counter increments across every glob of every territory in one flattened sequence, not per-territory, so a glob's tiebreak index depends on how many globs precede it across ALL prior territories, not just its own.

sameAsClassOf deliberately ignores retraction so a node that deriveSameAs no longer merges (because its bridging edge was retracted) is still returned as a member of the door's authorization class, meaning the governance gate charges against the pre-retraction class even after the read-side relation has split.

del(a, _k) ignores its key argument entirely and simply returns the archive unchanged for any input — it is not a conditional refusal that checks anything about the key, it is an unconditional identity function.

SCN-MEM-7f-1 calls store.attemptDelete on 'R1', a rule inserted at wave 1 whose ledger holds just one hit that has decayed across 9 subsequent waves (so it is almost certainly already evicted to the archive by wave 10) — the delete still throws, showing the rejection applies uniformly regardless of whether the targeted rule is currently active or already archived.

resolveExportFor returns null for a name that IS a genuine externally-called export elsewhere in the index when queried against a different unit that does not own it, rather than resolving it against the other unit's definition.

The test proves worldScope defaulting to scope produces output that is byte-for-byte identical (via toEqual on the whole data object) to explicitly passing world equal to scope, not merely that both happen to reach the same verdict string.

In decideMechanisms, once a site escalates (highValue && uncertain), 'self-consistency' is always added unconditionally, while 'check-synthesis' and 'refuter' are each gated by separate, independent conditions (checkable+tier, and tier==='T0' respectively) that can each be true or false independently of the other.

the raw-NUL check reads the source file's bytes with `indexOf(0)` on the Buffer rather than decoding it to a string first and searching that, specifically because a lone 0x00 byte survives UTF-8 decoding as U+0000 and could otherwise be missed by a decoded-string search.

In callTool's relations branch, a non-string `direction` argument is silently coerced to undefined (the default), while a malformed STRING direction is instead passed through to relationsVerdict for rejection — the two invalid shapes are handled at different layers.

admit() refuses a 'runtime' check kind (e.g. an endpoint-returns-200 behavior) as non-evaluable just like a 'code-exec' kind, so any runtime-behavior check is forced down the advisory path rather than becoming a live predicate node.

With budget ceiling 0, the default multi-arm run still emits three separate 'mine: 0 candidate facts' why-empty lines, one verbatim per arm heading, rather than deduplicating the identical empty-arm diagnostic into a single shared explanation.

soleHomeViolations flags a value only when its homes array is EXACTLY {'pr-attachment'}; a value whose homes is a superset (e.g. {'trailer','pr-attachment'}) passes even though pr-attachment is still one of its homes.

For alice, who is entitled to honest answers, the store-health and pair-state axes each yield a distinct non-'unauthorized' refusal reason (three total), while the existence axis alone still collapses to 'unauthorized' even for her — so the collapse is a decision applied to one specific axis, not a general refusal to disclose anything to an authorized caller.

importCas's content-address integrity check (rejecting a body not addressed by its filing key) only fires for keys that are hash-shaped; an entry filed under a non-hash-shaped key like asHash('abcd') is carried through verbatim with no re-derivation check at all, so the integrity guard is conditional on key shape rather than universal over every object in the bundle.

An import statement at the top of a file is excluded entirely from the folded item children — the fold captures top-level declarations only (functions, classes, const/let), not every top-level statement.

ratioOf returns 0 both when a territory has no matching tally at all and when it has a tally with total===0, so a territory that was never tallied reads as a perfect 0% unresolved ratio rather than as an error or an undefined/unknown value, and gate() therefore reports such a territory as PASS.

correspondence's keyOfSubtree map resolves ties by lexicographically-smallest key when the same subtreeHash appears under multiple node-identity keys, because the pairs are sorted by (subtreeHash, key) ascending before the first-wins insertion into the map.

materializePoke writes only the canonicalForm bytes of the source's raw Pack|Poke surface to disk — the seat identifier appears solely in the output filename (`<seat>.poke.json`), never encoded into the written bytes themselves, so the file's content alone does not identify which seat it was materialized for.
TranscriptRef.store is constrained to exactly three literal values: 'lfs', 'partial-clone', or 'cas'.

auditClaimScrub/auditCheckScrub operate on raw source-code text passed as a string (the mutants are inline JS-source template literals, never imported or executed modules), so the audit is a purely static/syntactic check that does not require the mutant code to type-check or run.

The 'ghost' test proves that a projection row whose contentHash does not resolve in CAS is silently dropped from the pack rather than surfaced or causing a throw: cover('src') returns zero invariants and the call itself does not throw.

The property test's 'scope' set used to determine expected underApprox includes the query node q itself (unioned with rc.closure), so an unresolved/dynamic edge sourced from q counts toward underApprox even though q is asserted to never appear in rc.closure itself.

every structural mutant in this suite (restore, hydrate, raw, forget) is inserted via the exact same anchor string, `fetch(ref: TranscriptRef): Transcript {`, so all four new-method mutants are spliced into the source immediately before the same fetch method rather than at distinct locations.

CurrentNode's seal field, when absent, is documented to mean the seal is UNKNOWN rather than meaning the fact is not proven, so callers must not treat a missing seal as an implicit false/unproven verdict.

describeFreshness('FRESH') mentions 'interface' in its rendered text, reflecting that FRESH means both the fact's own hash AND its dependencies' interfaces are unchanged, not just the fact's own content.

A successful assert-mode link() result has no `retracted` key at all in its returned object (verified via toEqual against an object literal that omits the field entirely), not a `retracted: false`, so existing consumers reading LinkOut see byte-identical shape to before retraction was added.
init's territory lines are rendered SORTED alphabetically by name regardless of the input array's order, so a territories list arriving as [zeta, alpha] still prints alpha before zeta.

The first-time and idempotent-rerun cases of `atlas init` are distinguished by two entirely different stdout substrings ('gitignore:' when the rule is newly written vs 'already denied' when it is already present), rather than the same message appearing both times.

The revision hash passed to every emit() call in this file (AT) is literally the value NaN cast through 'as unknown as Hash', so every seal-carry assertion in this suite runs with a bogus, non-hash rev argument and still admits — meaning the gate/grounding check here does not meaningfully validate that argument.

isUntrustedStore takes the trust-check function itself rather than a boolean, and treats an ABSENT seam as trusted (returns false), so a runtime built without provenance wiring at all behaves as if the store were trustworthy.

asHash, asSubtreeHash, and asNodeKey perform no runtime validation whatsoever — each is a bare `s as Brand` cast that accepts any string, including an empty string or one that is not a valid hash format, and mints it as the branded type.

MarginalValueStop is declared as its own standalone interface with literal types (window: 20, minAdmits: 4) but is NOT a field on GenesisBudget or DeepeningLoops — it exists purely as a documented fixed policy at the type layer, separate from the budget shape a caller actually constructs.
abstainedFromWire discards the entire abstention ledger (falling back to {}) if even a single entry in the wire array is malformed, rather than dropping only the bad entry.

A committed policy.json with a JSON key literally named '__proto__' under scopes is tested to load without rebinding the parsed scopes object's prototype (it stays null), proving the loader constructs scopes as a null-proto map rather than assigning into a plain object literal (which would fire the __proto__ setter).

The class-(a) test proves a schema-violating argument is rejected as malformed-args at the handler layer before the underlying tool leg is ever invoked: it wraps the leg to increment a counter and asserts that counter is still 0 after the call.

The MALFORMED refinement local test shows the mint escapes a local component that itself contains an embedded '::' and a trailing ':' wholesale into a single segment, rather than splitting on the local's own internal '::' — the minted key has exactly two '::'-segments, not three.

pullTail takes the unrolled `root` object directly as its first argument rather than the already-computed rollup result `a`, so fetching a facet's pull-reachable tail does not require having called rollup() at all.

A row whose tier is off-lattice (outside the recognized T0-T3 governance tiers used by the two bands) is excluded from both the invariants and advisory bands and is also excluded from advisoryDropped and pullReachable, so it leaves no trace at all in the briefing's truncation accounting.

ground() fails closed at the WHOLE-FACT level, not per-citation: if even one of a fact's citations is unresolvable, the entire returned grounding has zero entries (not just the resolvable citations surviving alone), so a fact with two citations where only one dangles ends up completely ungrounded rather than partially grounded.

keyOf() computes the identical nodeKey for two facts at the same anchor even when their `scope` fields differ in both type and value (an array vs. the string 'core'), directly demonstrating that scope plays no role at all in the node-key derivation.

toGitPointer produces an object with exactly two keys, `sha` and `store`, and the `store` value is the literal string 'cas' — the pointer never carries any transcript body bytes, only the content hash and a fixed store discriminant.

parseModelConfig only checks that costCapNum and costCapDen are both positive integers given together — it never validates that the ratio is sensible (e.g. num <= den), so a config with costCapNum > costCapDen (a cost cap over 1.0) is accepted without complaint.

The rank oracle's tie-break order is tier, then ppr descending, then distance ascending, then nodeKey — so ppr dominates distance in the ordering, meaning a farther node with higher ppr (e_hub at distance 2) outranks a closer node with lower ppr (e_leaf at distance 1) at the same tier.

decideStaging scrubs a relation's or negation's identity-bearing fields (endpointA/endpointB, target/scope) individually before minting the row, so re-deriving relationKey/negationKey from those same scrubbed values externally reproduces the row's actual nodeKey byte for byte.

pairKey encodes an unordered pair as `${lo.length}:${lo}${hi}` (length-prefixed, no separator character), rather than joining the two strings with a delimiter, so the split point is recovered from the numeric prefix instead of being searched for inside the concatenated payload.

buildSound unconditionally stamps seal:'proven' regardless of whether witnessOf returns a witness or undefined, so the type-expressible GEN-12k arm (which has no target/scope legs and therefore no witness) still gets the same proven seal as the dependency/count/definition arms that do carry a re-provable witness.

hotSet()'s over-budget flag uses a strict greater-than comparison (size > budget), so a hot-set whose size exactly equals the budget is NOT flagged over — only strictly exceeding the budget trips the advisory.
In buildGate, the gateHolds function receives an `_at: Hash` parameter that is never referenced in its body, so the rev/sha argument passed to it plays no role in computing the returned verdict.

clone() calls exportCas(cas) directly rather than calling the exportStore() helper defined later in the same file, even though exportStore is just a one-line wrapper around exportCas doing the identical serialization.

relationSetFor excludes a candidate dependent fact from the dependents list whenever that fact's own anchor already lies under the queried scope, treating it as the unit's own content rather than something that depends on it, even though it was reached via the scope's blastRadius entry.

governingGotchas evaluates atLeastT1 using a hardcoded 'FRESH' freshness placeholder rather than the caller-supplied freshnessOf oracle, unlike governingInvariants and advisoryBand which both call freshnessOf(row.fact) for the same tier check.

isScope checks `typeof v === 'string'` before ever checking length, so it rejects a String wrapper object, a Symbol, an array, or any object with a coercing toString/valueOf outright, without ever reaching a comparison that would coerce such a value.

reconcileModelCalls() returns 0 across every scenario in this suite, including both the golden cases and the 200-run property test that varies domain author, override, and tier, confirming reconcile never invokes a model regardless of manifest listing or override state.

The returned targetEscapes lookup sorts its witness-sites array before returning it, so the witnesses come back in lexical order rather than in the document-scan order they were discovered/appended in.

This test statically re-reads store.ts's own source at runtime and asserts its import lines never mention routeWrite or upsert, enforcing that rehydrateProjection cannot depend on the routing seam by construction, not merely by spying on the put() call count during one rehydrate run.

A pass can stage a second claim about the same symbol it already staged in an earlier upsert within the same run, and both claims land on the SAME minted nodeKey with claims appended in order, rather than the second claim being excluded because the symbol appears to already exist in the snapshot.

id({rId, status, freshness}) with two different status/freshness values still produces the SAME hash (asserted directly with different 's'/'X' and 2/9), proving canonicalForm silently strips the status/freshness fields from any preimage rather than merely ignoring them by convention.

SCN-TOOLS-14c-1 supplies a pull hook that THROWS if ever invoked, and asserts pullCalls stays 0 after onTransition, so the test proves the boundary push path never even attempts to call pull, rather than merely tolerating a pull failure or an unavailable harness.

put(scrub(bytes)) and put(bytes) always yield the same content hash, since the store scrubs every input before addressing it, so a caller who pre-scrubs before calling put gets no different result than one who does not.

The commit retry loop is bounded at exactly 64 attempts: when a rival writer wins the compare-and-swap on every single attempt, the emit door makes exactly 64 tries (asserted via `expect(n).toBe(64)`) before giving up and returning the `contended` refusal with nothing written.

mkGate's gateHolds only consults isGrounded/freshness when the incoming candidate status is exactly 'HOLDS'; any other incoming status is returned completely unchanged without ever calling isGrounded, so a downgrade can only ever happen starting from HOLDS.

SCN-GEN-2d-1's big-frontier case uses gateEmitAll (100% admit rate) specifically so the marginal-value halt never triggers, isolating the hard ceiling: with a 500-site frontier it asserts calls.length is exactly 200, not merely <=200, proving the ceiling is reached and not cut short by the marginal-window logic under full admission.

A Grounding with one valid entry and one entry carrying an undefined subtreeHash is refused entirely by both isGrounded implementations rather than partially accepted, so a single bad entry among several good ones sinks the whole grounding.

The test asserts exactly 3 separate lines containing 'atlas doctor index' (one per arm), not a single shared guidance line, proving each of the three arms (advisory/dependency/count) emits its own independent why-empty next-step rather than one message printed once for the whole run.

cov.gate returns false to signal a FAILING gate under this suite's stated polarity convention (true=PASS), so a caller checking gate() must not read a plain false as 'not applicable' — it means the coverage ceiling was crossed.

the shallow-clone TOTALITY test deliberately clones at depth 2 rather than depth 1, because probeHistory checks commitCount before shallowness, so a depth-1 clone would trip the low-commit-count branch first and never reach the shallow-clone check this test targets.

IndexNode deliberately has no `ppr` field even though a personalized-PageRank rank is a lead-ratified stored value elsewhere, because no reference scopes that field to IndexNode or Rollup, so PPR must live on some other record.

The relationKind vocabulary check in negationKey is case-sensitive: the uppercase variant 'CALLS' of the valid lowercase kind 'calls' is rejected as off-vocabulary, not silently normalized or accepted.

bindSubtree applies canonicalForm to the unit BEFORE handing it to encoder.hash (asSubtreeHash(encoder.hash(canonicalForm(unit)))), so the injected Encoder itself receives already-canonicalized bytes and is never responsible for canonicalizing its own input.

legWired treats a leg as wired whenever handle() does NOT return the specific 'not wired at this seam' rejection string, so a leg that is present but fails for its own domain/argument reasons still counts as wired — the same as one that fully succeeds.

main()'s promise itself rejects (not resolves to some non-zero exit code) when the thrown error is off the mine-catch's allow-list, unlike the allow-listed and success cases which both resolve to a numeric exit code — so a foreign error changes main's settlement kind, not just its return value.

admit() rejects an assertion expr with more than 3 pipe-delimited parts (parts.length !== 3), but evalAssertion itself only destructures the first three parts and silently ignores any extras, so calling evaluate() directly (bypassing admit) on such a malformed expr still produces a real HOLDS/BROKEN verdict rather than NA.
stageRowWithoutBytes stages a row using the fact's REAL content address (the same hash a normal stage would compute), simulating a pruned CAS rather than a fabricated or malformed hash.

A malformed `anchors` field inside `authz` causes parseAuthz to return undefined, which propagates through parsePolicy to discard the ENTIRE policy (including the otherwise-valid `scopes` and `t0Heuristic` legs) and fall back to defaultPolicy, rather than degrading just the anchors binding to absent.

mergedPack over multiple territories shares ONE PACK_CAP token budget across all of them combined, not a separate PACK_CAP allotment per territory, so packing K territories together yields a strictly smaller total than packing each one individually.

objFingerprint mints a node's state fingerprint through the sealed id() seam over a structured {objects} preimage rather than joining the objects array into one string, specifically because a separator-joined fingerprint would let a value crossing an array-index boundary collide (e.g. ["a b"] and ["a","b"] would fingerprint identically under string-joining).

The concurrency test's child-process writer imports the store implementation from a compiled dist path (dist/src/store.js) rather than the .ts source, since spawned Node subprocesses cannot import TypeScript directly.

A bare-directory primaryAnchor 'src/' (trailing slash, no filename) satisfies the scope-containment binding trivially because unitScopeOf strips the trailing slash as if it were a filename component, so this case is caught only by the separate document-existence check, not by the scope check.

promoteVerdict distinguishes an unreadable staging read (read:false) from an honestly empty one (read:true, candidates:0) with different exit codes (2 vs 0) and different stdout text, explicitly asserting the unreadable case's output does NOT contain the phrase used for the empty case ('staging holds no candidates').

makeFixRepo writes the UNTRACKED files (dist/bundle.js, debug.log) to disk before running git add, relying on the committed .gitignore to exclude them from the commit rather than simply never writing them at all.

the `dep-F` pool key is the sole entry in the UNCAPPED set, so it is the only one of the seven capped pools (dep-T, neg-T, neg-F, cnt-T, cnt-F, rel-T, rel-F) exempted from the SEM_BENCH_CAP truncation and is instead measured exhaustively.

isEvent's guard checks only that `supersedes` is an Array via Array.isArray, without validating the type of any element inside it, so append() will admit an event whose supersedes array holds arbitrary non-Hash values.

consult() returns an empty array, not the full entry list, when the query object has none of the recognized filter keys (prId/date/territory) — an unfiltered or unrecognized query yields nothing rather than everything.

Configuring the proposer as the `true` binary (exit 0, empty stdout) makes a real pass genuinely count as 2 llmCalls while every site abstains, demonstrating the CLI treats an empty-stdout model response as a real proposer call rather than as evidence no model is wired.

headByContentHash filters entries to only those that are fresh AND have an empty supersedes array before taking the max by contentHash, so a fresh entry that supersedes another entry would be excluded from head selection even though it is marked fresh.

The sealed kernel createStore()'s own put() silently returns the empty string '' (not undefined, not a throw) when handed an object carrying a float like confidence:1.5, as directly demonstrated by the PREMISE test calling createStore().put() with no wrapper involved.

A gitignore file where the Atlas rule lines are commented out (prefixed with '#') is treated as though the rule were entirely absent — outcome 'installed', matching a fresh file's outcome — not 'partial-repaired' or 'already-present', because the matcher compares exact trimmed line text rather than substring containment.
supersede checks addressability only on the OLD node's CAS put; the new/superseding node is never put through the store or checked for addressability at all — it is returned unchanged.

negationsOf reads a negation's `target` field off `node.endpointB` rather than off a dedicated negation-specific property, so the negation row's target identity leg physically lives on the same carrier a relation row uses for its second endpoint.

seededCount falls back to r.seeded.length only when the report has no coverage ledger at all (ledgerSeededIds returns undefined) — a report that has a coverage ledger but whose sites are all outcomes other than 'seeded' would report 0 from the ledger rather than falling back to r.seeded.length.

KINDS, the order budget() rows emit in, is Object.keys(BASE_CAP) SORTED — this reorders the eight InjectionKind entries alphabetically rather than preserving the declaration order they were written in (awareness, orientation, projectMem, own, pack, protocols.safetyCritical, protocols.advisory, poke).

poisonedRepo's put() function writes the forged CAS object and projection.json directly to disk with writeFileSync, never calling createGovernedEmit or any other door, so the forged fact enters the repo without passing through any gate the runtime otherwise enforces.

The audit's hasScrub flag only guards against a totally-absent scrub() call (NO-SCRUB); a mutant that calls scrub(...) but assigns its result to an unused variable while storing the raw answer elsewhere still passes the hasScrub check yet is separately caught by the per-site data-flow check (CAS-ID-NOT-SCRUBBED/STORED-OBJECT-NOT-SCRUBBED), showing the two checks are independent, not one implying the other.

When retract is given a string value instead of a boolean, the handler rejects it as malformed-args and v.data is asserted to be undefined, proving the echoing atlas-link leg is never invoked at all for a type-invalid retract argument.

seedGate's verdict object omits the `obviousness` field entirely (rather than setting it to undefined) when no ObviousnessScore argument is passed, verified by the test asserting `'obviousness' in seedGate(c)` is false.

objectReason's per-property loop only validates a declared property when it is present in the argument bag (`if (!(key in bag)) continue`), so this module never flags a missing required field itself — that case is covered only by the separate missingRequiredReason function invoked on the throw path.

isHash validates only that a value's typeof is 'string', with no length or hex-format check, so render() would treat an empty string as a well-formed sha and pass it through to source.diff() unrejected.

ratify() only special-cases the T0 tier; any staged candidate whose tier is not T0 (T1, T2, or anything else) commits with any non-empty token.by string, so the function's tier-branch logic treats every non-T0 tier identically.

evaluate() distinguishes an unrecognized index-query operator from a recognized-but-failing one: an unknown op like 'unrecognized-op|x' yields NA, while a well-formed 'exists|...' query against a genuinely absent target yields BROKEN, rather than both collapsing to the same verdict.

The provableFirst stable-partition reorder inside createMine is only correctly honored because the downstream mine.ts call site passes runExtract a single-site array; if a caller ever routed the whole multi-site ranked frontier through runExtract (which sorts ppr-primary), that reorder would be silently undone.

The 'refused slot left NO node behind' test deliberately keeps a console.log of the served rows in the committed test code (with an eslint-disable-next-line no-console comment) rather than removing the debug print, so the test's own output shows the query rows on every run.

marshalLink has no way to explicitly request retract:false — any supplied value for --retract other than 'true' (including the literal '--retract=false') is refused as a marshal error, so the only way to assert (retract:false) is to omit the --retract flag entirely.
doors.nonObvious is hardcoded to always return false, so this admission gate scores every mined claim as 'obvious' unconditionally rather than computing any real signal for it.

The `node` builder keys its entries Map by `contentHash`, so if two Events passed to it share the same contentHash but differ in id/payload/seq, only the LAST one in the input array survives in the resulting Node — the earlier one is silently overwritten rather than both being retained.

The fold-merge head resolution for two colliding events with identical seq values (both seq=5 in the direction-independence test) still deterministically picks a winner purely by comparing contentHash strings, proving seq plays no role in head selection even when it is equal across the two candidates.

the `set()` helper deduplicates by event id using `if (!m.has(e.id)) m.set(...)` (first-write-wins on id collision), so this file's fixtures rely on every event id being unique across g/h/i/w/x rather than on the map's natural last-write-wins overwrite semantics.

captureModelIdentity's --version probe discards stderr entirely (stdio: ['ignore','pipe','ignore']), so a failing binary's error message is never captured into the identity string — only the generic 'probe failed' note is.

rangeOf(OTHER, 'greet', 2) is used to locate the occurrence for OTHER.ts's GREET symbol, deliberately picking the SECOND textual match of 'greet' in that file (the call site 'return greet()') rather than the first match, which falls inside the import statement 'import { greet } from ...'.

The class-(a) test shows the CLI's argv marshalling for `reconcile` cannot itself produce a type-invalid `--by` value (the parser folds it to a string), so the malformed-args case can only be reached by calling handler.handle directly with a raw envelope, bypassing the CLI's own argv path entirely.

bindFreshness collapses the oracle's 3-state grounding Freshness down to 2 states by treating anything other than the literal string 'FRESH' as DRIFTED, so a STALE verdict from the injected oracle would also read as DRIFTED here rather than being distinguished.

the tampered-body-under-an-honest-key test builds its forged import dump by JSON.stringify'ing a literal `{format:'atlas-okf', version:1, objects:{...}}` object directly rather than by calling exportCas() and mutating its output, so the envelope shape it exercises is hand-written to match the importer's expectations rather than derived from the real exporter.
tierRank inverts STRICTNESS's numbering so T0 ranks 0, T1 ranks 1, and T2 ranks 2, while an unrecognized value ranks last at TIER_COUNT (3) rather than first.

For a 3-citation fact, dropping any single one of the three citations (index 0, 1, or 2) always makes the whole ground() result unGrounded, so the fail-closed-per-fact behavior holds regardless of WHICH citation position is lost, not just for a specific subset.

The parse-tolerant 'ceiling' arm filters dynamicReach witnesses by string-suffix match on exactly two tags (':unparsed' and ':js-unscanned'), dropping only those two fail-closed categories while treating every other witness suffix as a real dynamic channel.

gate.gateHolds only ever downgrades a verdict, never upgrades: a non-HOLDS verdict like 'advisory' or 'BROKEN' passes through completely unchanged even when the grounding is valid and fresh, so the gate cannot promote a weaker verdict to HOLDS on its own.

precomputedConfig treats its seven precomputed fields asymmetrically: axes/rawTree/fileTree/scipOutput/symbolReverse are always spread in unconditionally, while indexerName/targetEscapes/dynamicReach are conditionally omitted from the object entirely when their computed value is undefined.

Committing only .atlas/projection.json makes 'query' exit 0 (narrowed, not refused), while committing only .atlas/staging.json makes the same 'query' exit 2 with an untrusted-store refusal, so which of the two sidecar files was accidentally tracked determines whether a read is served or refused.

Unlike reverifyRelation and reverifyFact, which each check that an anchor/endpoint scope aligns with the witness's own scope before replay, reverifyNegation performs no such anchor-scope binding check at all — it only checks target/scope non-emptiness and that the scope still has documents.

Of the six LangId values declared (ts, py, go, java, rust, rb), REAL_INDEXER only configures entries for ts and py — planIndexers routes every other language straight to the HONEST_HOLE sentinel with empty args.

gate.gateHolds never reads the fact's own stored freshness field at all: the test deliberately mis-stamps a genuinely fresh, HOLDS-worthy fact's freshness to 'DRIFTED' and gateHolds still returns 'HOLDS', proving the field is completely inert at the emit door regardless of its value.

specDropOrder's warm-vs-cold branch is decided per call by checking whether ANY row in the passed-in rows array has hits > 0 (`rows.some((r) => r.hits > 0)`), not by a separate flag, so a mixed batch with only one nonzero-hits row is still classified entirely as 'warm' and sorted by hitRate rather than falling back to cold-start order.

Three of this suite's four cases assert by reading compose.ts/policy.ts source text with readFileSync and checking string containment (exact substrings/sentences), rather than exercising any runtime behavior of the code under test.

The strict unknown-flag refusal is scoped to the 'link' command only: 'query --nonsense' and 'reconcile --whatever' both still succeed (ok:true), silently ignoring the unrecognized flag, so the marshaller's strictness is per-command rather than a shared, uniform property of the CLI.

The wrong-directory refusal test proves the injected reverify thunk is never invoked (calls stays 0) and exits 2 when cwd lacks .atlas/, while the adjacent test proves an existing-but-empty .atlas/ DOES invoke the thunk (calls becomes 1) and exits 0 — the same 'no work found' surface text is reachable through two behaviorally distinct paths.

partition() silently drops an entry from every bucket (added/edited/superseded/decayed) whenever provOf(signal) returns undefined, even after the entry was already routed into a specific bucket by the head-comparison logic — so a provenance-less change produces no visible diff entry at all rather than an error.

SCN-INDEX-12a-1 changes only the node's status field (active to stale) between the two createRollup calls while holding freshness fixed at the same value (1) in both, so the assertion that rId stays unchanged is demonstrated only for a status change, not for a change to the freshness value.

PHANTOM never appears anywhere in the INDEX fixture array (neither as a define nor a reference entry), so its unresolvability in the test comes purely from total absence from the index rather than from an explicit rejection record.

Ref is a union of StructRef OR a bare string, so any field typed Ref (grounding, ref, links) can be either a structured path@subtreeHash anchor or an unstructured pointer string, and a consumer cannot assume the structured shape without a runtime check.

casObjects() counts on-disk CAS entries by filtering the recursive directory listing to names containing a '/', which deliberately excludes the bare two-character shard subdirectory entries themselves and counts only the nested value files inside them.

routeWrite's valid output set never includes a REJECT decision — the exhaustive product test over all 16 (contentHashHit x nodeKeyHit x family x checkSame) combinations asserts every cell lands in {DEDUP, CREATE, UPDATE, SUPERSEDE}, confirming admission/rejection is handled entirely outside this routing function.

For a carried-forward row (contentHash unchanged), stampGeneration prefers the incoming `row.derivedAt` over the previous generation's `before.derivedAt` via `??`, checking the NEW row's own stamp first rather than always trusting the prior generation's recorded stamp.

Setting ATLAS_MINE_BUDGET to a positive integer doesn't just cap the site count — resolveMineBudget also turns OFF all three deepening loops (review, enrich, expand) on the returned budget, so a capped run cannot deepen on any site even ones within the ceiling.

The fixture oracle treats an anchor whose qualifiedPath is absent from the current tree as unresolvable and defaults it to DRIFTED rather than FRESH, so a missing key fails closed instead of being treated as unchanged.
Only ./types.js is re-exported with the type-only form (`export type *`); all fifteen other runtime modules listed in this barrel are re-exported with a plain value `export *`.

persistProjection admits an NFC/NFD key-collision row and round-trips BOTH keys with their distinct values intact (nothing is dropped), because the two normalized forms are distinct byte sequences that JSON.stringify/parse both preserve as separate object keys — the row becomes unaddressable by id rather than lossy.

the crux test's two fixtures both cite identical anchors A and B with identical subtreeHash 'sh'/'sh-door', so the emit-vs-refuse split between the relation fact and the intrinsic-advisory fact is driven purely by the fact's `kind`/shape (relation vs advisory with two grounding entries), not by any difference in the grounded content itself.
Of the four declared credential families, only aws-access-key-id has a `ceiling` field (16, equal to its floor), so its body length is bounded while the other three families' bodies are unbounded.

marshalArgs('init', [], {}) called directly with zero positionals still succeeds and defaults path to '.', a code path this test file's own comment says is otherwise unreachable through main() since parse enforces an init positional.
The BOTH-is-default test verifies the omitted-direction output is byte-for-byte string-equal to the explicit 'both' output, not merely that both calls succeed or return the same edge count.

The test suite sets process.env.ATLAS_RATIFY_TOKEN even though the fact is T1 (not T0), and its own comment notes a T1 fact routes to full-ratify and is visible in reads, implying full-ratify is not reserved to T0 facts alone.

the fixture's SCIP occurrence ranges are computed by rangeOf locating the n-th plain-text occurrence of an identifier substring in the source string, not by any AST or tree-sitter-derived position, so the ranges fed into the test are purely string-search-derived even though the code under test consumes tree-sitter grammars.

answerReceipt never calls store.put itself; it only computes id(obj), the same id store.put would return, so the actual CAS persistence of `obj` depends entirely on a separate caller pushing it onto the mine pass's own put array.

seedGate builds two structurally different SeedDecision object literals depending on whether obviousness is undefined, rather than always including an `obviousness` key set to undefined, so the key is entirely absent from the object rather than present-but-undefined when no score is supplied.

adapter.territories() synthesizes a fixed owner of the empty string and a single glob pattern `${name}/**` for every territory returned, rather than reading owner/glob data from the underlying @atlas/index territory axis at all.

classify() checks isStagingPath before isProvableStorePath, so a repo where BOTH staging and projection/cas files are tracked by git always classifies as 'tracked-staging' (the flat refusal), never 'tracked-provable', regardless of how much provable material also rode along.

reconcile checks the unaccounted (dropped-site) condition before the duplicates condition, so a ledger with BOTH dropped sites and duplicate rows reports only the dropped-sites 'DOES NOT CLOSE' reason and never mentions the duplicates in its `why` string, even though the returned `duplicates` array is still populated.

The nodeKey-identity test attaches `seal` to the candidate via a runtime cast ('as unknown as Candidate') rather than as a declared Candidate field, and confirms nodeKey(proven) === nodeKey(noSeal) — proving nodeKey's computation ignores a seal value present on the object at runtime, not merely absent from the type.

createFileSourceReader refuses to read a file whose final path component is a symlink unconditionally — even one that resolves to another ordinary file inside the same repository — rather than only refusing symlinks that escape the repo.

The published `atlas-query` schema's `by` property is asserted to be a closed 3-value enum of exactly ['scope', 'dependency', 'trigger'], and a call with any other value (e.g. 'graph') is refused as malformed input on both the CLI and MCP transports rather than silently falling back to the default 'scope' mode.

modelCalls is incremented by the FULL dispatched batch.length before the per-site fold loop even runs, so when a lower-ranked site faults and higher-ranked batch-mates get discarded, modelCalls still counts those discarded calls even though llmCalls and budgetSpent (incremented only inside the fold) do not.

COMMAND_LIST, the human-readable list of valid commands shown in every ParseError message, omits 'transitions' and 'transition' even though both are valid keys in the ARITY table with their own required-positional counts — a user who mistypes either command never sees it listed as a valid option in the error.
nextLine computes its `facts` count by summing invariants, gotchas, and advisory rows together, so a scope holding only unratified advisory rows is not treated as having no fact filed.

SCN-MEM-10b-1 constructs a Substrate fixture with seatBrief/llmOutputs/toolIO but immediately voids it with `void substrate` and never passes it into respawnFromRecord or any assertion, so the rebuild in that test is proven using only the versioned MemoryStore record, not the substrate object it builds.

relationsVerdict checks unit for emptiness before validating rawDirection, so a call with BOTH an empty unit AND an out-of-vocabulary direction always returns the 'missing unit' rejection and never surfaces the direction error at all.

closedSlotRefusalText describes a non-string offending slot value by its KIND (e.g. 'an array', 'a number value') rather than interpolating the value itself into the message, specifically to avoid a crafted object's toString() impersonating a legitimate slot name in the rendered text.

the mirror pin imports MINED_TIER from `@atlas/adapter-io`'s package root rather than from reverify-store.ts directly, so the test verifies the value as re-exported on adapter-io's public barrel surface, not by reaching into the specific internal module that declares the mirrored literal.
The scorer reports falseAdmit as null (not 0) for an arm that has zero rows, so an empty arm is distinguishable from an arm that was measured and found to have a genuine 0% false-admit rate.

An unsealed fact is entirely out of scope for the tracked-provable reverify pass: of the 4 seeded facts (one unsealed), sealedProven counts only 3, so the unsealed row is neither served nor counted as broken/unverifiable — it is simply excluded from the pass's population.

answersStored is counted per-fact by whether a rawAnswer was actually attached, not by the number of admitted/seeded facts: a pass whose gate admits facts with no rawAnswer at all reports a positive seeded count but answersStored strictly 0.

The test compares realpathSync of both the observed repo path and the temp repo rather than comparing the raw strings, specifically to tolerate macOS resolving process.cwd() through a /var/folders to /private/var/folders symlink.

The totality test for `get` checks two distinct miss shapes — the empty-string sentinel AND a well-formed-looking 64-character all-zero hex hash — rather than relying on the empty-string case alone to prove misses are handled honestly.

Pack has an advisoryDropped counter for the advisory band's cap but no analogous dropped-count field for the invariants (governing) band, so the type gives no way to honestly report a truncation of the governing band the way it does for the advisory one.

ROUTER_EDGES contains only one edge whose `to` is 'ratified', and its `via` is 'interview' rather than 'write' — so canAutoPromote's hardcoded false is also independently verifiable by filtering the edge array itself for a to:'ratified' edge with via:'write', which does not exist.
