groundedMultiSymbolFact wraps its nodeKey(candidate) call in a try/catch and, if minting throws, substitutes the fixed literal string 'author-could-not-mint' as the fact's id rather than propagating the error, letting the helper still construct and return a degenerate-anchor fact object that the real product's identity minting refused.

makeGitlabishForge's bareClone() implementation copies only the commits map (via writeCommit) into the fresh forge and never touches the prs map at all, so a cloned forge always starts with zero PR-side data regardless of how many PRs the original forge held.

stageCandidate reads claimNorm via an unchecked cast `(f as {claimNorm:string}).claimNorm`, so calling it with a 'relation'-kind GroundedFact (which carries no claimNorm field) would silently produce a WriteRequest with claimNorm: undefined rather than failing — nothing in this function's control flow guards against that kind.

SCN-GL-15 and SCN-GL-16 assert full-buffer equality via Buffer.compare(healthy, pruned) in addition to comparing the extracted reason string, so any change to the rejection message's surrounding prose (not just the reason field) would fail these tests even if the reason stayed the same.

The snapshot object returned by log.append exposes a mutating delete() method (it is called directly on `snap`), but invoking it has no effect on later append calls' view of the log, since the next snapshot still contains the deleted event.

scipState distinguishes 'absent' from 'unreadable' purely by testing the caught error's message against the regex /ENOENT/ — any other thrown error, including a corrupt-protobuf parse failure, is classified as 'unreadable' with the raw message preserved rather than 'absent'.

gitYieldMs blocks the calling thread synchronously via Atomics.wait on a SharedArrayBuffer word that is never signaled, so the wait always runs the full requested duration rather than being interruptible/resolved early by any notify.

orderDroppable computes the warm/cold decision once for the entire call by checking whether ANY row has hits>0, not per-kind, so a single kind with nonzero hits flips every other kind — even ones with zero hits of their own — from the cold-start tie-break comparator to the hitRate-asc comparator.

freshness()'s multiset comparison is order-insensitive (a reordered closure with the same multiset still reads FRESH) but treats interfaceRState as part of a member's identity, so two occurrences of the same node with different interfaceRState values are NOT counted as matching duplicates.

The authz policy only scopes 'src' for the ACTOR, yet emitting a relation whose object endpoint (vendor/lib.ts) lies entirely outside any declared scope still succeeds (exit 0), so the write door's authz check for a relation is not gated on the object endpoint's own directory being in scope.

isSemanticSlot performs an explicit typeof-string check before consulting SEMANTIC_SLOT_SET, so it is total over any unknown input (numbers, objects, undefined) and returns false rather than throwing when handed a non-string value, unlike a bare Set.has(x as string) cast would be.

The wrong-shape sidecar test notes that dropping only the Array.isArray guard (without also removing the surrounding try/catch) leaves the test green, because the try/catch alone already covers the resulting TypeError — so the guard is defense-in-depth, not the property actually exercised by that mutant alone.

createUnitDepCandidates and createDepResolver each independently call createUnitDeps(scip) on the same ScipOutput, building two separate UnitDepsApi instances rather than sharing one, even though both are meant to be used together (prompt-side candidates and gate-side resolution) over the same scip data.

buildNegation's placeholder grounding is a structurally well-formed { entries: [] } (an empty but present entries array), not null or undefined, so any downstream code that only checks 'grounding is present' rather than 'entries is non-empty' would treat the un-overwritten placeholder as satisfied.

A JS-family file (.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs) is unconditionally flagged as a dynamic-reach channel witness regardless of its actual contents — even one containing none of the five tracked constructs — because this scanner only parses the TS grammar and never inspects JS file bytes at all.

A negation grounded on a directory anchor drifts not only when a new sibling file is inserted into the scope, but also when the byte content of an EXISTING file already in the scope changes with no files added or removed, since any child hash change propagates up into the directory's own folded subtreeHash.

pathSegments both trims whitespace from each individual segment AND silently drops empty segments produced by a double slash, so ' a / b //c ' normalizes to exactly ['a','b','c'] rather than preserving an empty segment for the doubled slash.

a dependency-axis leaf's subtreeHash is set to asSubtreeHash(h) where h is literally the same value as the leaf's own key, so this axis's leaf hashes are structurally constant under content edits and can never register drift on their own, unlike the spatial/territory axes whose hashes fold real node content.

resolveDepFor returns null both for a symbol a unit merely doesn't reference (like 'statSync' for pay) and for a symbol the unit itself defines (like 'Hash' for contracts.ts), treating self-definition and non-reference as the same null outcome rather than distinguishing them.

sameAsEdgeState reads as 'retracted' from EITHER endpoint even when only one node's row carries the retraction marker (kA has sameAsRetracted:['kB'] but kB's mirror never landed), so the read path does not require both sides of a pair to have written the retraction to honor it.

Passing a sibling reader (related) to createPromptFactory together with a template that lacks a {{RELATED}} placeholder throws a PromptError immediately at factory construction time, rather than silently building a prompt that drops the sibling context.

byUnitPrior and compareSiteOrder both break exported/bytes ties in the SAME direction (exported sorts before unexported, and larger bytes sorts before smaller), but compareSiteOrder adds a 'sub' leg immediately after 'group' so a file site always sorts before its own sub-file units within the same group, a distinction byUnitPrior has no analog for since it only compares units within one file.

the suite's stated boolean polarity is true=PASS, so gate() encodes a FAILing verdict as the literal `false`, and both SCN-INDEX-16b-1 and SCN-INDEX-16c-1 assert `cov.gate(t0)` equals `false` for the ceiling-crossing case rather than `true`.
When ATLAS_MINE_SLOT is unset, driveMineArms runs the pass exactly three times in the fixed order advisory, dependency, count — not some other order or a set of concurrent/unordered calls.

SCN-INDEX-12i-1 and SCN-INDEX-12j-1 call only fold.rehashState(A), without a preceding fold.propagateDirty(A) call, and still observe correct eager-rehash results and state-suspect marking on the distant nodes, so rehashState alone is sufficient to produce those effects rather than requiring the caller to invoke propagateDirty first.

itemsOf (the AST-fold path used by foldAstUnits) parses the raw file src directly without ever calling normalizeForGrammarGaps, unlike parseTsDoc in this same file which always normalizes first, so the three known grammar-gap constructs still fail-close to an empty item list on the fold path even though parseTsDoc would rescue them.

The callsSeam regex probe explicitly excludes a match like `store.admitToBuffer(a, b)` (a method call on some other object) from counting as a real caller of the module-level admitToBuffer function, via a negative lookbehind for a preceding dot or word character.

The EncoderApi interface declares a wrapper shape `{ readonly encoder: Encoder }`, but nothing in this file actually implements or exports a value typed as EncoderApi — `defaultEncoder` is exported directly typed as the bare `Encoder`, not nested under an `encoder` field.

auditRelationScrub/auditNegationScrub are STATIC audits over source text, not runtime tests of executed code: the 'mutant' cases are hand-written template-string snippets of JS that are never imported or run, and the 'shipped file is clean' cases feed the raw text of mine-decide.ts read via readFileSync, so the audit inspects code shape (which function calls flow into which variables) rather than executing decideStaging.

foldArms computes its ratified total via a genuine reduce-sum over every arm's report.ratified.length rather than a hardcoded zero, even though every arm's mine pass is candidate-only and the sum is currently always zero.

gateWithPresent's gateHolds function explicitly checks `node.kind === 'advisory'` before comparing claimNorm against the present set, so passing it any non-advisory GroundedFact (e.g. a predicate node) always returns 'NA' regardless of whether anything matching would have been in the set.

serve() calls ctx.port.postMessage before Atomics.add/Atomics.notify on the completion counter, not after, so the main thread — which wakes on the counter — is guaranteed the answer message was already posted by the time it wakes and drains the port.

the test proves callTool has no membership gate by calling it with the literal string 'atlas-not-a-real-tool' and asserting handler.seen equals exactly that one name — i.e. callTool forwards an entirely fabricated, off-surface tool name straight to handler.handle rather than rejecting it before dispatch.
